  10: 
  11: ## The rule
  12: A new pattern, repo, SDK, or external primitive is ADOPT-NOW only when CONVERGENCE evidence is present. Convergence means the pattern exists independently in multiple authoritative places, not just one. Absent convergence, the default verdict is **REJECT-until-convergence** — not STUDY-PILOT, not "maybe later."
  13: 
  14: This gate stacks ABOVE the `.claude/skills/sota-research/SKILL.md` 5-row LOAD-BEARING bar (LOCAL — sota-research skill present at `.claude/skills/sota-research/SKILL.md`). It is stricter: the 5-row bar allows STUDY-PILOT on any `[UNKNOWN]`; the convergence gate does not — any missing convergence axis is a REJECT until that axis is satisfied OR the STRONG-PROVENANCE-EXPRESS predicate fires.
  15: 
  16: ## Convergence axes (ALL three required for ADOPT-NOW)
  17: 
  18: | Axis | Threshold | Evidence shape |
  19: |---|---|---|
  20: | **Independent T1 sources** | ≥3 distinct orgs/repos/papers implementing the pattern | file:line cites in 3 different `Z:/repos/deps/<repo>/` dirs OR 3 different official docs URLs — not 3 pages of the same source |
  21: | **Named T2 practitioners** | ≥2 named practitioners publicly adopting | Recognizable engineers (Karpathy / Simon Willison / Boris Cherny / Anthropic staff / equivalents), with a dated artifact (tweet, blog post, commit, conf talk) citing THIS specific pattern — not generic category endorsement |
  22: | **Stability** | ≥3 months from pattern emergence to evaluation date | first public commit/post ≥90d old; <90d = "new and shiny," re-evaluate after the burn-in period (UNLESS STRONG-PROVENANCE-EXPRESS applies — see §Axis 3 5-band table) |
  23: 
  24: Any axis failing = REJECT-until-convergence. Verdict line must name the specific missing axis + the exact evidence that would satisfy it.
  25: 
  26: ## Terminology disambiguation
  27: 
  28: **Convergence-gate Axis 3** = **stability** (age + cpd; quantitative scalar measuring repo/pattern maturity). About: "is this pattern old enough to trust?"

  85: 
  86: | Tool family | Use | Status |

  92: **Rule**: 90 days minimum from EARLIEST public artifact, not from the version you're looking at. A v2.0 release isn't stability evidence if v1.0 was 30 days ago.
  93: 
  94: **Supplementary signal — commits/day (cpd)**: raw age alone under-specifies stability. A 99-day-old repo shipping 15 commits/day is structurally different from a 99-day-old repo shipping 1 commit/week — the former is still in active iteration, not burn-in. Compute `cpd = total_commits / age_days` alongside age:
  95: 
  96: | cpd × age band | Classification | Implication |
  97: |---|---|---|
  98: | `cpd < 10` AND `age ≥ 90d` | Stable burn-in | Firm axis-3 PASS |

 100: | `cpd > 10` AND `age > 180d` | **Sustained active maintenance** | Firm axis-3 PASS — mature age proves stability AND velocity signals ongoing investment, NOT rewrite churn. Classic shape: high-velocity repos past burn-in (avoid misclassifying as fast-churn anti-pattern) |
 101: | `cpd > 10` AND `age < 100d` | Fast-churn anti-pattern | Treat age-PASS as borderline, expect rewrites, re-audit after +90d |
 102: | **STRONG-PROVENANCE-EXPRESS** (5th band, predicate-gated): `age ≥ 30d` AND axis-1 = official-org maintainership AND axis-2 = named-T2 endorsement OR maintainer-org IS T2-equivalent | **Firm axis-3 PASS — relaxed maturity gate** | When provenance is strong (org-level T1) AND a named-T2 OR org-equivalent endorsement exists, the launch-spike risk that motivates the strict 90-day gate is dominated by maintainer-org commitment. The LAUNCH-SPIKE band still applies for `unknown-org + age<90d + cpd>50` — protection holds for the truly anti-pattern cases (solo-org launch with non-permissive license = REJECT-UNTIL-CONVERGENCE unchanged) |

If 3 cheap signals converge, don't escalate to expensive ones; if they don't converge, ONE expensive confirmatory signal is worth more than three more cheap ones.

 112: ## Anti-pattern: retroactive convergence manufacturing
 113: 
 114: Do not construct convergence evidence after choosing the verdict. The sequence must be: (1) collect convergence evidence → (2) count axes → (3) verdict. Not (1) pick verdict → (2) find supporting cites.
 115: 
 116: If a candidate looks promising but fails convergence today, the right move is to **queue a re-audit date** (90 days out, or when a named T2 practitioner is spotted adopting it), not lower the gate.

 118: ## Anti-pattern: Row-2 fabrication-test FAIL
 119: 
 120: When running the 5-row bar's Row 2 (Numeric — measurable improvement), a README presenting **≥3 numeric performance claims without methodology citation** (no repro script link, no benchmark repo, no dataset name) is **auto-FAIL** — do not attempt live A/B to verify, just REJECT. This short-circuits the primary-source rule: vendor marketing numbers that aren't backed by a reproducible artifact are false-by-default until proven otherwise.
 121: 
 122: **Procedure**:
 123: 1. Count numeric claims in README that make improvement/speedup assertions
 124: 2. For each, check: does the README cite a reproducible artifact (benchmark script path, dataset name, tool+version)?
 125: 3. If ≥3 claims lack citations, Row-2 auto-FAIL → REJECT verdict bypasses expensive verification step
 126: 4. If 1-2 claims lack citations, run the live-verify anyway (lower signal-to-noise)
 127: 5. If all claims cite reproducible artifacts, proceed to full primary-source check
 128: 
 129: **Why auto-FAIL not just downgrade**: across multiple prior live A/B verifications of fabrication-pattern candidates, none survived verification. The prior probability of "≥3 unsourced claims yet verifiable" is empirically near-zero. Running the bench is budget-wasting ritual.

  36: rtk filters and compresses command outputs before they reach your LLM context. Single Rust binary, 100+ supported commands, <10ms overhead.
  37: 
  38: ## Token Savings (30-min Claude Code Session)
  39: 
  40: | Operation | Frequency | Standard | rtk | Savings |
  41: |-----------|-----------|----------|-----|---------|
  42: | `ls` / `tree` | 10x | 2,000 | 400 | -80% |
  43: | `cat` / `read` | 20x | 40,000 | 12,000 | -70% |
  44: | `grep` / `rg` | 8x | 16,000 | 3,200 | -80% |
  45: | `git status` | 10x | 3,000 | 600 | -80% |
  46: | `git diff` | 5x | 10,000 | 2,500 | -75% |
  47: | `git log` | 5x | 2,500 | 500 | -80% |
  48: | `git add/commit/push` | 8x | 1,600 | 120 | -92% |
  49: | `cargo test` / `npm test` | 5x | 25,000 | 2,500 | -90% |
  50: | `ruff check` | 3x | 3,000 | 600 | -80% |
  51: | `pytest` | 4x | 8,000 | 800 | -90% |
  52: | `go test` | 3x | 6,000 | 600 | -90% |
  53: | `docker ps` | 3x | 900 | 180 | -80% |
  54: | **Total** | | **~118,000** | **~23,900** | **-80%** |
  55: 
  56: > Estimates based on medium-sized TypeScript/Rust projects. Actual savings vary by project size.

  68: ```bash

  71: 
  72: > Installs to `~/.local/bin`. Add to PATH if needed:
  73: > ```bash
  74: > echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc  # or ~/.zshrc
  75: > ```
  76: 
  77: ### Cargo
  78: 
  79: ```bash
  80: cargo install --git https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk
  81: ```

  83: ### Pre-built Binaries
  84: 
  85: Download from [releases](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk/releases):
  86: - macOS: `rtk-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` / `rtk-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz`
  87: - Linux: `rtk-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` / `rtk-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz`
  88: - Windows: `rtk-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip`
  89: 
  90: > **Windows users**: Extract the zip and place `rtk.exe` somewhere in your PATH (e.g. `C:\Users\<you>\.local\bin`). Run RTK from **Command Prompt**, **PowerShell**, or **Windows Terminal** — do not double-click the `.exe` (it will flash and close). For the best experience, use [WSL](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install) where the full hook system works natively. See [Windows setup](#windows) below for details.

README=Z:\repos\deps\cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\README.ko.md
   1: # claude-code-cache-fix
   2: 
   3: [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/claude-code-cache-fix?color=blue)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/claude-code-cache-fix) [![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-18%2B-green)](https://nodejs.org/) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/cnighswonger/claude-code-cache-fix)](https://github.com/cnighswonger/claude-code-cache-fix/stargazers)
   4: 
   5: [English](./README.md) | [中文](./README.zh.md) | 한국어 | [Português](./docs/guia-pt-br.md)
   6: 
   7: [Claude Code](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code)용 캐시 최적화 프록시입니다. 과도한 쿼터 소모를 유발하는 프롬프트 캐시 버그를 수정하고, 요청 접두사를 안정화하며, 자동 회귀를 모니터링합니다. v2.1.113+ Bun 바이너리를 포함한 모든 CC 버전에서 동작합니다.
   8: 
   9: > **v3.0.3** — 7개 핫리로드 확장을 갖춘 로컬 HTTP 프록시입니다. v2.1.117에서 A/B 테스트 결과: 첫 번째 웜 턴에서 **프록시 경유 95.5% 캐시 히트율 vs 직접 연결 82.3%**. [전체 릴리스 노트 →](https://github.com/cnighswonger/claude-code-cache-fix/releases/tag/v3.0.0)
  10: 
  11: > **Opus 4.7 주의사항:** 계측 데이터에 따르면 4.7은 동일한 가시 토큰 수 대비 **Q5h 쿼터를 4.6의 약 2.4배 속도로 소모**합니다([@ArkNill이 독립 확인](https://github.com/ArkNill/claude-code-hidden-problem-analysis/blob/main/16_OPUS-47-ADVISORY.md)). 두 가지 요인: 새 토크나이저(최대 35% 더 많은 토큰, [문서화됨](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/whats-new-claude-4-7))와 적응적 사고 오버헤드(약 105%, 사용량 응답에 미문서화). Q5h 영향은 **Q7d**(대부분의 헤비 유저가 먼저 도달하는 주간 쿼터 상한)에 복리로 누적됩니다. 우회 방법: `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE_THINKING=1`을 설정하면 소모율이 약 3.3배 감소하지만, 복잡한 작업에서 품질이 떨어질 수 있습니다. [Discussion #25](https://github.com/cnighswonger/claude-code-cache-fix/discussions/25)(초기 관찰)와 [Discussion #42](https://github.com/cnighswonger/claude-code-cache-fix/discussions/42)(통제된 A/B 데이터 + Q7d 분석)를 참조하십시오.
  12: 
  13: ## 빠른 시작: 프록시 (권장)
  14: 
  15: 프록시는 모든 CC 버전(Node.js 또는 Bun 바이너리)에서 동작합니다. Claude Code와 Anthropic API 사이에 위치하여 핫리로드 확장으로 캐시 수정을 적용합니다.
  16: 
  17: ```bash
  18: # 설치
  19: npm install -g claude-code-cache-fix
  20: 
  21: # 프록시 시작 (localhost:9801에서 실행)
  22: node "$(npm root -g)/claude-code-cache-fix/proxy/server.mjs" &
  23: 
  24: # 프록시를 경유하여 Claude Code 실행
  25: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9801 claude
  26: ```
  27: 
  28: 이것으로 완료입니다. 프록시가 7개 캐시 수정 확장을 자동으로 적용합니다. 래퍼 스크립트, `NODE_OPTIONS`, 프리로드가 필요 없습니다.
  29: 
  30: ### 프록시의 동작
  31: 
  32: 모든 `/v1/messages` 요청에 7개 확장이 순서대로 실행됩니다:
  33: 
  34: | 확장 | 수정 대상 |
  35: |------|----------|
  36: | `fingerprint-strip` | 시스템 프롬프트에서 불안정한 cc_version 핑거프린트를 제거합니다 |
  37: | `sort-stabilization` | 도구 및 MCP 정의의 결정적 순서를 보장합니다 |
  38: | `ttl-management` | 서버 TTL 티어를 감지하고 올바른 cache_control 마커를 주입합니다 |
  39: | `identity-normalization` | 접두사 안정성을 위해 메시지 ID 필드를 정규화합니다 |
  40: | `fresh-session-sort` | 첫 번째 턴의 비결정적 순서를 수정합니다 |
  41: | `cache-control-normalize` | 메시지 간 cache_control 마커를 정규화합니다 |
  42: | `cache-telemetry` | 응답 헤더에서 캐시 통계를 추출하여 `~/.claude/quota-status.json`에 기록합니다 |
  43: 
  44: 확장은 핫리로드됩니다 — `proxy/extensions/`에서 `.mjs` 파일을 추가, 제거 또는 수정하면 프록시 재시작 없이 다음 요청부터 적용됩니다. 설정은 `proxy/extensions.json`에 있습니다.
  45: 
  46: ### 서비스로 실행
  47: 
  48: **Linux (systemd — 권장):**
  49: 
  50: `~/.config/systemd/user/cache-fix-proxy.service`를 생성합니다:
  51: 
  52: ```ini
  53: [Unit]
  54: Description=Claude Code Cache Fix Proxy (v3.x)
  55: After=network.target
  56: 
  57: [Service]
  58: Type=simple
  59: ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/node /path/to/claude-code-cache-fix/proxy/server.mjs
  60: Restart=on-failure
  61: RestartSec=5
  62: Environment=CACHE_FIX_PROXY_PORT=9801
  63: 
  64: [Install]
  65: WantedBy=default.target
  66: ```
  67: 
  68: ```bash
  69: systemctl --user daemon-reload
  70: systemctl --user enable --now cache-fix-proxy
  71: 
  72: # 선택: 로그인 전 부팅 시 시작
  73: sudo loginctl enable-linger $USER
  74: ```
  75: 
  76: `cache-fix-proxy install-service` 서브커맨드는 v3.1.0에서 계획 중입니다([#48](https://github.com/cnighswonger/claude-code-cache-fix/issues/48)).
  77: 
  78: **폴백 (모든 OS):**
  79: 
  80: ```bash
  81: nohup node "$(npm root -g)/claude-code-cache-fix/proxy/server.mjs" > /tmp/cache-fix-proxy.log 2>&1 &
  82: echo 'export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9801' >> ~/.bashrc
  83: ```
  84: 
  85: ### 상태 확인
  86: 
  87: ```bash
  88: curl http://127.0.0.1:9801/health
  89: # {"status":"ok"}
  90: ```
  91: 
  92: ## 빠른 시작: 프리로드 (CC v2.1.112 이하)
  93: 
  94: Node.js 기반 CC 버전(v2.1.112 이하)을 사용 중이라면 프록시 없이 프리로드 인터셉터를 사용할 수 있습니다:
  95: 
  96: ```bash
  97: npm install -g claude-code-cache-fix
  98: NODE_OPTIONS="--import claude-code-cache-fix" claude
  99: ```

README=Z:\repos\deps\motiful-cc-cache-audit\README.md
   1: # cc-cache-audit
   2: 
   3: Claude Code v2.1.69+ injects a dynamic billing header into the system prompt that breaks cross-session prompt cache sharing. This repo contains the A/B test that proves it and the one-line fix.
   4: 
   5: ## The Fix
   6: 
   7: ```bash
   8: echo 'export CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER=false' >> ~/.zshrc
   9: source ~/.zshrc
  10: ```
  11: 
  12: Only affects new sessions. Existing ones keep running fine.
  13: 
  14: ## Root Cause
  15: 
  16: Since v2.1.69, Claude Code prepends an `x-anthropic-billing-header` string to the system prompt:
  17: 
  18: ```
  19: x-anthropic-billing-header: cc_version=2.1.88.a3f; cc_entrypoint=cli; cch=00000;
  20: ```
  21: 
  22: That `.a3f` suffix is a 3-char SHA-256 hash computed from the first user message in each conversation:
  23: 
  24: ```javascript
  25: // Deobfuscated from cli.js
  26: function computeHash(firstUserMessage, version) {
  27:   const chars = [4, 7, 20].map(i => firstUserMessage[i] || "0").join("");
  28:   return sha256("59cf53e54c78" + chars + version).slice(0, 3);
  29: }
  30: ```
  31: 
  32: Different conversation → different first message → different hash → different system prompt prefix.
  33: 
  34: This also affects **subagents within the same conversation**. Each Agent tool call has its own message context, so its first "user message" (the agent prompt) produces a different hash. Verified in a real session — 3 distinct hashes in one conversation:
  35: 
  36: ```
  37: Main conversation:  cc_version=2.1.88.a3f  (34 API calls)
  38: Subagent 1:         cc_version=2.1.88.e91  (3 API calls)
  39: Subagent 2:         cc_version=2.1.88.7c2  (3 API calls)
  40: ```
  41: 
  42: Anthropic's prompt cache uses [prefix matching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching) with no per-session isolation — cache is shared at the Organization/Workspace level. So all Claude Code sessions and subagents *should* share the same cached system prompt. But the billing header makes each one's prefix unique, causing the system prompt (~12K tokens) to get rebuilt from scratch every time.
  43: 
  44: ## A/B Test
  45: 
  46: 4 sessions per round, each with a different prompt, sequential with 8-second gaps (within the 5-min cache TTL). All sessions use `claude --print` mode.
  47: 
  48: ### Round A — Header ON (default)
  49: 
  50: | Session | Prompt | cache_read | cache_creation | hit ratio |
  51: |---------|--------|-----------|----------------|-----------|
  52: | 1 | What is the capital of France? | 11,272 | 12,206 | 48.0% |
  53: | 2 | List three prime numbers under 20. | 11,272 | 12,202 | 48.0% |
  54: | 3 | Explain what a goroutine is in one sentence. | 11,374 | 12,753 | 47.1% |
  55: | 4 | Name one benefit of TypeScript over JavaScript. | 11,272 | 12,203 | 48.0% |
  56: 
  57: Every session rebuilds ~12K tokens of cache.
  58: 
  59: ### Round B — Header OFF
  60: 
  61: | Session | Prompt | cache_read | cache_creation | hit ratio |
  62: |---------|--------|-----------|----------------|-----------|
  63: | 1 | What is the capital of France? | 23,478 | 0 | 99.98% |
  64: | 2 | List three prime numbers under 20. | 23,474 | 0 | 99.98% |
  65: | 3 | Explain what a goroutine is in one sentence. | 11,272 | 12,197 | 48.0% |
  66: | 4 | Name one benefit of TypeScript over JavaScript. | 23,475 | 0 | 99.98% |
  67: 
  68: 3 out of 4 sessions: zero cache creation, full cache read. Session 3 was a server-side cache eviction — cache came right back for session 4.
  69: 
  70: ### What the Numbers Mean
  71: 
  72: The data shows a two-tier caching pattern, consistent with the Anthropic API's cache hierarchy (`tools → system → messages`):
  73: 
  74: - **Tools block (~11,272 tokens)**: Tool definitions are stable across sessions — always cached regardless of header setting.
  75: - **System prompt block (~12,200 tokens)**: Contains the billing header with a per-session hash — rebuilt every session when header is ON.
  76: 
  77: With the header OFF, both blocks are fully cacheable → 99.98% hit ratio.
  78: 
  79: ### Cost Impact
  80: 
  81: Using Anthropic pricing (cache_read = 0.1x base, cache_creation = 1.25x base):
  82: 
  83: | | Header ON (per session) | Header OFF (per session) |
  84: |--|----------------------|------------------------|
  85: | Effective cost | 11,272×0.1 + 12,200×1.25 + 3 ≈ **16,380 equiv tokens** | 23,475×0.1 + 0 + 3 ≈ **2,351 equiv tokens** |
  86: | | baseline | **~85% reduction (~7x cheaper)** |
  87: 
  88: This measures system prompt cost only. For long conversations where user messages dominate, the relative savings decrease.
  89: 
  90: ## FAQ
  91: 
  92: **Will this get me banned?**
  93: 
  94: No reports of anyone being banned or warned. [claude-code-router](https://github.com/musistudio/claude-code-router/pull/1220) and [CLIProxyAPI](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/issues/1592) ship with this disabled in production. The env var is a proper feature toggle in the source code.
  95: 
  96: **Why did Anthropic add this?**
  97: 
  98: Internal billing attribution — tracking which Claude Code version and entrypoint (CLI, SDK, GitHub Action) made each API call. It's in the system prompt instead of HTTP headers probably because Bedrock/Vertex don't forward custom headers. The API has a `metadata` field designed for exactly this kind of thing.
  99: 
 100: **Do I need to restart existing sessions?**

  52: 
  53: ## What is Claw Compactor?
  54: 
  55: Claw Compactor is an open-source **LLM token compression engine** built around a 14-stage **Fusion Pipeline**. Each stage is a specialized compressor — from AST-aware code analysis to JSON statistical sampling to simhash-based deduplication — chained through an immutable data flow architecture where each stage's output feeds the next.
  56: 
  57: ### Demo
  58: 
  59: ```
  60: $ claw-compactor benchmark ./my-workspace
  61: 
  62:   Claw Compactor v7.0 — Fusion Pipeline Benchmark
  63:   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  64: 
  65:   Scanning workspace... 47 files, 234,891 tokens
  66: 
  67:   Stage Results:
  68:   ┌──────────────────┬──────────┬───────────┬──────────┐
  69:   │ Stage            │ Applied  │ Reduction │ Time     │
  70:   ├──────────────────┼──────────┼───────────┼──────────┤
  71:   │ Cortex           │ 47/47    │ —         │ 12ms     │
  72:   │ Photon           │ 3/47     │ 2.1%      │ 4ms      │
  73:   │ RLE              │ 41/47    │ 8.3%      │ 6ms      │
  74:   │ SemanticDedup    │ 47/47    │ 12.7%     │ 18ms     │
  75:   │ Ionizer          │ 8/47     │ 71.2%     │ 9ms      │
  76:   │ Neurosyntax      │ 23/47    │ 18.4%     │ 31ms     │
  77:   │ TokenOpt         │ 47/47    │ 4.1%      │ 3ms      │
  78:   │ Abbrev           │ 12/47    │ 6.8%      │ 5ms      │
  79:   └──────────────────┴──────────┴───────────┴──────────┘
  80: 
  81:   Summary:
  82:     Before:  234,891 tokens ($2.35 at GPT-4 rates)
  83:     After:   108,250 tokens ($1.08)
  84:     Saved:   126,641 tokens (53.9%) — $1.27/run
  85:     Time:    88ms total
  86: 
  87:   Estimated monthly savings at 100 runs/day: $3,810
  88: ```

  42: ## Overview
  43: 
  44: - OpenAI/Gemini/Claude compatible API endpoints for CLI models
  45: - OpenAI Codex support (GPT models) via OAuth login
  46: - Claude Code support via OAuth login
  47: - Amp CLI and IDE extensions support with provider routing
  48: - Streaming, non-streaming, and WebSocket responses where supported
  49: - Function calling/tools support
  50: - Multimodal input support (text and images)
  51: - Multiple accounts with round-robin load balancing (Gemini, OpenAI, Claude)
  52: - Simple CLI authentication flows (Gemini, OpenAI, Claude)
  53: - Generative Language API Key support
  54: - AI Studio Build multi-account load balancing
  55: - Gemini CLI multi-account load balancing
  56: - Claude Code multi-account load balancing
  57: - OpenAI Codex multi-account load balancing
  58: - OpenAI-compatible upstream providers via config (e.g., OpenRouter)
  59: - Reusable Go SDK for embedding the proxy (see `docs/sdk-usage.md`)
  60: 
  61: ## Getting Started
  62: 
  63: CLIProxyAPI Guides: [https://help.router-for.me/](https://help.router-for.me/)
  64: 
  65: ## Management API
  66: 
  67: see [MANAGEMENT_API.md](https://help.router-for.me/management/api)
  68: 
  69: ## Usage Statistics
  70: 
  71: Since v6.10.0, CLIProxyAPI and [CPAMC](https://github.com/router-for-me/Cli-Proxy-API-Management-Center) no longer ship built-in usage statistics. If you need usage statistics, use:
  72: 
  73: ### [CPA Usage Keeper](https://github.com/Willxup/cpa-usage-keeper)
  74: 
  75: Standalone persistence and visualization service for CLIProxyAPI, with periodic data sync, SQLite storage, aggregate APIs, and a built-in dashboard for usage and statistics.
  76: 
  77: ### [CLIProxyAPI Usage Dashboard](https://github.com/zhanglunet/cliproxyapi-usage-dashboard)
  78: 
  79: Local-first usage and quota dashboard for CLIProxyAPI. It collects per-request token usage from the Redis-compatible usage queue into SQLite, visualizes daily and recent-window usage by account and model, and shows Codex 5h/7d quota remaining in a local web UI.
  80: 
  81: ## Amp CLI Support
  82: 
  83: CLIProxyAPI includes integrated support for [Amp CLI](https://ampcode.com) and Amp IDE extensions, enabling you to use your Google/ChatGPT/Claude OAuth subscriptions with Amp's coding tools:
  84: 
  85: - Provider route aliases for Amp's API patterns (`/api/provider/{provider}/v1...`)
  86: - Management proxy for OAuth authentication and account features
  87: - Smart model fallback with automatic routing
  88: - **Model mapping** to route unavailable models to alternatives (e.g., `claude-opus-4.5` → `claude-sonnet-4`)
  89: - Security-first design with localhost-only management endpoints
  90: 
  91: When you need the request/response shape of a specific backend family, use the provider-specific paths instead of the merged `/v1/...` endpoints:
  92: 
  93: - Use `/api/provider/{provider}/v1/messages` for messages-style backends.
  94: - Use `/api/provider/{provider}/v1beta/models/...` for model-scoped generate endpoints.
  95: - Use `/api/provider/{provider}/v1/chat/completions` for chat-completions backends.
  96: 
  97: These routes help you select the protocol surface, but they do not by themselves guarantee a unique inference executor when the same client-visible model name is reused across multiple backends. Inference routing is still resolved from the request model/alias. For strict backend pinning, use unique aliases, prefixes, or otherwise avoid overlapping client-visible model names.
  98: 
  99: **→ [Complete Amp CLI Integration Guide](https://help.router-for.me/agent-client/amp-cli.html)**

  15: 
  16: ## The rule
  17: 
  18: Sota-researcher / architect / general agent dispatches that surface SOTA candidates MUST include a **harness-fit verification step** asking "is this applicable to OUR specific architecture?" — beyond the convergence-gate Axis 1+2+3 (T1 sources / T2 practitioners / Axis 3 stability) that scores SOTA-status. Without harness-fit, candidates pass convergence-gate AND still fail at ship-target verification because of architectural mismatch invisible to upstream-source-only audit.
  19: 
  20: This is **convergence-gate Axis 4** (harness-fit) — separate from Axis 1+2+3 (which classify SOTA-status of the candidate ITSELF) and applied AFTER convergence-gate PASS, BEFORE ship-target verification.
  21: 
  22: ## When this rule applies
  23: 
  24: Whenever an agent (sota-researcher / architect / general-purpose / Explore / code-reviewer / debugger) returns a ship-candidate ranking from a Wave-N dispatch:
  25: 
  26: 1. The agent's convergence-gate verdict is necessary BUT NOT SUFFICIENT for ship-readiness
  27: 2. The candidate may be valid SOTA AND inapplicable to claude-sota
  28: 3. Apply the 4-axis harness-fit probe BEFORE writing T1 consult prompt OR queuing the ship

  44: ## How to apply (4-axis probe)
  45: 
  46: Before declaring an agent's ship-candidate "ready":
  47: 
  48: ### Probe 1 — count-OVER
  49: 
  50: If the candidate claims a count delta (commit count, file count, line count, star count): verify against authoritative local source (`git log`, `wc -l`, `Glob | wc -l`, `mcp__github__search_repositories` star refresh) BEFORE accepting. Agent counts via remote APIs can drift, paginate-truncate, or include stale cache.
  51: 
  52: ### Probe 2 — SDK-vs-CLI surface
  53: 
  54: If the candidate proposes adopting an SDK feature / config flag / env var: verify the **invocation surface** exists in claude-sota:
  55: - Does claude-sota use the SDK or CLI? Check `.claude/hooks/scripts/*.py` + `.claude/settings.json` env block
  56: - Does the candidate's mechanism map to claude-sota's actual mode (interactive vs print-mode vs SDK-managed-agent)?
  57: - If the candidate requires a mode claude-sota doesn't run in, REJECT-for-fit even if SOTA-valid upstream
  58: 
  59: ### Probe 3 — architectural-API
  60: 
  61: If the candidate proposes a primitive (cache_control, prompt-cache, structured-outputs, batch-API): verify the **API ecosystem match**:
  62: - Anthropic-API primitive vs OpenAI-API primitive vs vendor-neutral OTel
  63: - claude-sota's gpt5.5/codex hooks talk to OpenAI-API endpoints; Anthropic-only primitives don't apply there
  64: - Cross-check before assuming "this Anthropic pattern works on codex"
  65: 
  66: ### Probe 5 — mode-harness-shape
  67: 
  68: If the candidate proposes adopting a skill/workflow/pattern with operational mode dependencies (HARD-GATE on user interaction, interactive-vs-autonomous mismatch, meta-skill assumptions about sister-harness presence, file-count or size-sprawl orthogonal to existing layout): verify the **operational mode + harness shape match**:
  69: - Does the candidate skill HARD-GATE on interactive user approval? Verify against claude-sota's autonomous /loop mode (incompatible)
  70: - Does the candidate require a sister-skill or sister-harness present in upstream's framework but absent locally? (e.g., Superpowers TDD-for-skills test framework)
  71: - Does verbatim port introduce file count or size disproportionate to existing layer? (e.g., a single skill bringing 7+ files when sibling skills are 1-3 files)
  72: - If ANY mode/harness assumption is unmet, REJECT-FOR-FIT even if SOTA-valid upstream + Axis 1+2+3 PASS
  73: 
  74: ### Probe 4 — plugin-namespace
  75: 
  76: If the candidate proposes vendoring an artifact from upstream (ECC, codex-plugin-cc, anthropics-cookbook): check **plugin-loaded skill namespace** FIRST:
  77: - `everything-claude-code:<artifact>` exposed via plugin? → DUPLICATE if vendored, REJECT per kiss-dry-yagni Must-Never #4
  78: - `codex:<artifact>` exposed via codex plugin? → DUPLICATE
  79: - `<plugin>:<artifact>` only available as legacy-shim? → still plugin-exposed
  80: - Only proceed with vendoring if the artifact is NOT in any loaded plugin namespace
  81: 
  82: **Where to check**: the available-skills list injected into agent context via system-reminder (lists every `<plugin>:<skill>` entry). Agents can also `mcp__github__get_file_contents` on the plugin's `marketplace.json` to enumerate exposed commands.
  83: 
  84: ### Probe 6 — supplementary direct-file/registry blockers (FM-09 promotion iter-67)
  85: 
  86: If the candidate proposes adopting an upstream artifact (skill, MCP server, plugin, library, vendored pattern) whose viability depends on:
  87: - License compatibility (claude-sota is permissive-license-only — MIT / Apache-2.0 / BSD acceptable; AGPLv3 / GPLv3 / SSPL / proprietary REJECT)
  88: - README badge / status banner (archive-status, deprecation notice, "moved to maintenance mode" warning)
  89: - Published-package existence (npm / PyPI / cargo / go-modules registry)
  90: - Build-deps availability (Cargo / GCC / Clang / Python venv requirement)
  91: 
  92: VERIFY via direct-file/registry probes:
  93: - **LICENSE file read** at upstream root: `cat Z:/repos/deps/<repo>/LICENSE | head -5` — match against permissive-license whitelist
  94: - **README badge inspection**: `rg -n "img.shields.io/badge/license|maintenance|archived|deprecated" Z:/repos/deps/<repo>/README.md`
  95: - **Registry direct-existence probe**: `curl -sS https://registry.npmjs.org/<pkg-encoded>` (`{"error":"Not found"}` = phantom) OR `curl https://pypi.org/pypi/<pkg>/json` (404 = phantom)
  96: - **Build-deps probe**: `which cargo gcc clang` OR check `pyproject.toml` / `package.json` for unsupported dep stack
  97: 
  98: If ANY direct-file/registry probe surfaces a blocker, REJECT-FOR-FIT even if SOTA-valid upstream + Axis 1+2+3 PASS + Probe 1-5 PASS. The blocker is STRUCTURAL — no operational mitigation exists.
  99: 
 100: **Empirical evidence n=2 (FM-09 ladder)**: Memory/RAG audit (openviking AGPLv3 LICENSE blocker — `reference_memory_rag_audit_HNF_agplv3_blocker_2026_05_02.md:52-64`); Ship D (ast-grep MCP phantom @anthropic/mcp-ast-grep npm package — `reference_ship_d_ast_grep_phantom_npm_HNF_2026_05_02.md`).

 102: ### Probe 7 — demand-gate split (NEW 2026-05-03; .a/.b sub-class added 2026-05-05 Wave 27 per Agent E §Issue 1 catch-22)
 103: 
 104: If the candidate proposes adopting a primitive (MCP / skill / library / tool) that is structurally sound (Probes 1-6 PASS): verify the **harness-side operational driver** BEFORE adoption. Probe 7 splits into two outcomes — `.a` REJECT (demand-absence) and `.b` STUDY-PILOT eligible (demand-creates-new-workflow). The split closes the Wave 27 catch-22 surfaced at `tmp/wave27-agentE-saturation-adversarial-2026-05-05.md:46-56,89-106` (Probe 7.a as currently worded auto-REJECTs any primitive that creates a NEW workflow because no sss invocation surface yet exists — circular per Jeffries YAGNI canonical statement at `kiss-dry-yagni.md:31-33`).
 105: 
 106: **Hard precondition (before applying .a or .b)**: earlier Axis-4 blockers WIN. If the candidate duplicates an existing shipped primitive (Probe 4 plugin-namespace), collides with plugin namespace, requires an unmet harness/mode assumption (Probe 5 mode-harness-shape), fails Probe 6 (license/registry/build-deps blocker), is SUPERSEDED-BY-X (existing primitive owns the workflow), or is a META-HARNESS competing-framework shape per `docs/verified-avoid.md` Cohort 1, classify under that blocker instead. Probe 7.b is ONLY available for structurally sound primitives that create a genuinely new, non-duplicative workflow.
 107: 
 108: #### Probe 7.a — DEMAND-ABSENCE (REJECT-FOR-FIT)
 109: 
 110: What sss workflow / invocation surface / consumer would route through this primitive TODAY? Verify the 3-clause check:
 111: - Cite a specific path (existing or queued)
 112: - Is the candidate's value proposition met by an EXISTING shipped primitive? (e.g., "graphiti MCP already provides FalkorDB temporal KG access" → dbhub adds no marginal value AS A REPLACEMENT)
 113: - Is the candidate displacing or extending? Displacement requires migration plan; extension requires marginal-value evidence
 114: 
 115: If NO current/queued workflow AND .b 5-clause check (below) does not survive, REJECT-FOR-FIT.a (demand-absence) — REJECT-decisive.
 116: 
 117: #### Probe 7.b — DEMAND-CREATES-NEW-WORKFLOW (STUDY-PILOT eligible)
 118: 
 119: A structurally sound primitive may create a genuinely new workflow that no existing sss primitive serves. STUDY-PILOT eligibility requires ALL 5 clauses to hold (codex T1 NEEDS-REVISION conf=0.84 Q2 prescription at `.claude/state/codex_consult_ship27_3_probe7_demand_creates_OUT.txt`):
 120: 
 121: 1. **Named operational use case**: cite the query/workflow and the consumer that would exercise it
 122: 2. **Cited local input/source path**: identify the concrete data, repo path, tool surface, or state file (e.g., `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/state/mcp_overhead_audit.jsonl`)
 123: 3. **Wiring path**: name the adapter/ETL/config needed to make the primitive consume the source; if wiring is non-trivial, it is part of the pilot cost
 124: 4. **Incumbent comparison**: explain why existing shipped primitives or simpler local commands (`rg`, `jq`, GitNexus, Langfuse MCP, graphiti, mcp-memory, one-off Python scripts) do not already satisfy the use case OR are materially worse
 125: 5. **Reversible time-box**: define owner, max pilot cost, 30-day success criterion, and retirement path
 126: 
 127: **Pilot failure**: retire to `disabledMcpjsonServers` if applicable and document in `docs/verified-avoid.md` under the matching failure cohort; create a dedicated retired-pilot / demand-not-realized cohort only after n>=2 same-shape recurrences. NOTE: `verified-avoid.md` Cohort 2 is specifically Probe 6 direct-file/registry blockers per `docs/verified-avoid.md:47-49`; failed demand-pilots do NOT belong there by default. Use the matching failure cohort for retirement (e.g., a pilot that failed because it duplicated an existing primitive retires to Cohort 1 META-HARNESS competing-frameworks).
 128: 
 129: **Example (dbhub Wave 27 caveat — ETL-explicit)**: bytebase/dbhub could enable SQL analytics over a generated SQLite audit warehouse derived from `.claude/state/*.jsonl`; the pilot must include the JSONL → SQLite ingestion path plus at least one committed query/report consumer. Without that ETL path, dbhub is NOT sufficient evidence for Probe 7.b — DBHub's official surface (`https://dbhub.ai/` + `bytebase/dbhub@72adfdcf` README + `server.json`) supports configured Postgres/MySQL/SQL Server/MariaDB/SQLite databases via SQL tools, NOT direct JSONL querying. Wave 27 codex T1 verified-via codex secondary probe of DBHub introduction page + TOML config docs + GitHub MCP-fetched README/server.json [VERIFIED 2026-05-05 via `.claude/state/codex_consult_ship27_3_probe7_demand_creates_OUT.txt`].

 131: **Harness-fit discriminator for REJECT vs STUDY-PILOT outcomes** (renamed from "4-class harness-fit-FAIL discriminator" per Wave 27 codex T1 Q1 prescription — `.b` is non-fail; original Q3 prescription at `.claude/state/codex_consult_axis4_subclass_taxonomy_probe7_demand_absence_OUT.txt:3825-3829` 2026-05-03; .a/.b split per Wave 27 codex T1 verdict at `.claude/state/codex_consult_ship27_3_probe7_demand_creates_OUT.txt` 2026-05-05): use BEFORE classifying a verdict to ensure the right Probe is invoked.
 132: 
 133: - `DEMAND-ABSENCE.a` (Probe 7.a): no current, queued, or counterfactual workflow survives the named-use-case check — REJECT-FOR-FIT
 134: - `DEMAND-CREATES-NEW-WORKFLOW.b` (Probe 7.b, NON-FAIL CLASS): structurally sound primitive creates a named, non-duplicative workflow; STUDY-PILOT eligible only after the 5-clause check passes
 135: - `SUPERSEDED-BY-X` (related to Probes 4/5): a workflow exists, but an incumbent primitive already owns it or was selected by prior verdict (e.g., cognee → Graphiti L3 verdict)
 136: - `PLUGIN-NAMESPACE` (Probe 4): the artifact already exists in a loaded plugin namespace
 137: - `MODE-HARNESS-SHAPE` (Probe 5): candidate requires an operating mode or harness assumption sss does not satisfy

 169: ### Codex-rescue blind-spot specialization (FM-09 promotion iter-67)
 170: 
 171: n=5 same-arc 2026-05-02 evidence ladder establishes that **codex-rescue agent (GPT-5.5 deep-dive variant) systematically returns ADOPT-NOW / STUDY-PILOT verdicts WITHOUT running Probe 4 / Probe 5 / Probe 6**. Pattern is agent-architecture-specific, not user-error: codex-rescue specializes in abstract-pattern reasoning (Axis 1+2+3 SOTA classification — T1 sources / T2 practitioners / Axis 3 stability) NOT repo-local-inventory reasoning (Axis 4 harness-fit). Different reasoning surfaces; codex-rescue's strength is the source of its blind-spot.
 172: 
 173: **The 2-stage validation contract** (n=5 base rate validated 100% on observable cases):
 174:

Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\CHANGELOG.md:158:- **BUGFIX: TTL ordering violation causes 400 error at Q5h=100%** — When the user's quota hit 100%, CC places `ttl: "5m"` markers. Our interceptor then added `ttl: "1h"` markers on other blocks, violating Anthropic's ordering constraint (1h cannot follow 5m in tools→system→messages order). Fix: detect existing TTL tier from the payload before any extension runs. If any block has `ttl: "5m"`, all injected markers (TTL injection, `cache_control_normalize`, `cache_control_sticky`) now use `5m` to match. Reported by @cowwoc (#44).

Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\CHANGELOG.md:172:- **BUGFIX: `cache_control_sticky` still exceeded 4-marker limit on CC v2.1.112** — v2.0.2 reduced `MAX_POSITIONS` from 3→2 assuming CC uses exactly 2 markers (1 system + 1 messages). CC v2.1.112 uses 3 markers in some configurations, so 2 sticky + 3 CC = 5, still exceeding the hard limit. Fix: count all existing `cache_control` markers across the full body (system + messages) before adding sticky markers, and cap the total at 4. No more assumptions about CC's marker budget. Caused `400 invalid_request_error` in production.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\CHANGELOG.md:174:16 total cache-stability fixes. 162 tests.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\CHANGELOG.md:178:- **BUGFIX: `cache_control_sticky` exceeded Anthropic's 4-marker limit** — Reduced `MAX_POSITIONS` from 3 to 2. With 1 system marker + 1 canonical from `cache_control_normalize` + 3 historical = 5, exceeding Anthropic's hard limit of 4 `cache_control` blocks per request. Caused `400 invalid_request_error` on sessions with enough history to fill all 3 slots. Now: 1 system + 1 canonical + 2 historical = 4.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\CHANGELOG.md:182:- **`cache_control_sticky`** — Preserves historical `cache_control` marker positions across turns. CC maintains one user-side marker at a time, dropping previous positions (~43 bytes of JSON framing per dropped position). On long sessions this causes tail-of-message byte drift that invalidates downstream cached blocks. This extension tracks up to 2 historical marker positions by stable message hash and reinstates them on subsequent turns (2 historical + 1 canonical from normalize + 1 system = 4, Anthropic's hard limit). Runs after `cache_control_normalize`. Credit: [@deafsquad](https://github.com/deafsquad) (PR #33).

Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\README.md:11:> **Opus 4.7 advisory:** Metered data shows 4.7 burns Q5h quota at **~2.4x the rate of 4.6** for equivalent visible token counts ([independently confirmed by @ArkNill](https://github.com/ArkNill/claude-code-hidden-problem-analysis/blob/main/16_OPUS-47-ADVISORY.md)). Two factors: a new tokenizer (up to 35% more tokens, [documented](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/whats-new-claude-4-7)) and adaptive thinking overhead (~105%, not documented in usage response). The Q5h impact compounds into **Q7d** — the weekly quota ceiling that most heavy users will hit first. Workaround: `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE_THINKING=1` reduces burn by ~3.3x but may reduce quality on complex tasks. See [Discussion #25](https://github.com/cnighswonger/claude-code-cache-fix/discussions/25) (initial observation) and [Discussion #42](https://github.com/cnighswonger/claude-code-cache-fix/discussions/42) (controlled A/B data + Q7d analysis).

Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\README.md:68:**Auto-recovery (Linux):** `install-service` also drops a healthcheck companion (`cache-fix-proxy-healthcheck.service` + `.timer`). The timer fires every 2 minutes; the oneshot service runs `curl -fs http://127.0.0.1:<port>/health` and `systemctl --user start cache-fix-proxy.service` if the probe fails. This recovers the proxy from any stop — clean or unclean, expected or unexpected — within 2 minutes. Background: `Restart=on-failure` doesn't fire on clean stops, so before this companion existed, a `systemctl stop` from any source (including unidentified ones during an Anthropic outage on 2026-04-25) would leave the proxy down indefinitely. macOS doesn't need the companion — launchd's `KeepAlive` already auto-restarts on any exit.

Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\README.md:204:**What it does:** Modifies outgoing request structure (block order, fingerprint, TTL, git-status) to fix cache bugs. Reads response headers and SSE usage data for monitoring.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\README.md:214:When you use `--resume` or `/resume` in Claude Code, the prompt cache breaks silently. Instead of reading cached tokens (cheap), the API rebuilds them from scratch on every turn (expensive). A session that should cost ~$0.50/hour can burn through $5–10/hour with no visible indication anything is wrong.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\README.md:218:1. **Partial block scatter** — Attachment blocks (skills listing, MCP servers, deferred tools, hooks) are supposed to live in `messages[0]`. On resume, some or all drift to later messages, changing the cache prefix.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\README.md:220:2. **Fingerprint instability** — The `cc_version` fingerprint (e.g. `2.1.92.a3f`) is computed from `messages[0]` content including meta/attachment blocks. When those blocks shift, the fingerprint changes, the system prompt changes, and cache busts.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\README.md:222:3. **Non-deterministic tool ordering** — Tool definitions can arrive in different orders between turns, changing request bytes and invalidating the cache key.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\README.md:249:cache-fix health: relocate=active(2h ago) fingerprint=dormant(5 clean sessions) tool_sort=active ttl=active identity=waiting
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\README.md:259:If cache_read ratio drops below 50% across 5+ calls after disabling fixes:
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\README.md:261:REGRESSION WARNING: cache_read ratio averaged 12% across last 5 calls.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\README.md:262:Fixes are disabled — consider re-enabling to recover cache performance.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\README.md:269:Before rewriting the `cc_version` fingerprint, the interceptor verifies that its hardcoded salt and character indices reproduce the fingerprint Claude Code sent. If verification fails (CC changed its algorithm), the rewrite is skipped automatically. This ensures the interceptor can never make cache performance *worse* than stock CC.

Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\README.md:317:Claude Code injects live `git status` into the system prompt on every call. Any file edit changes the git status, which busts the entire prefix cache. Disabling this saves ~1,800 tokens per call:
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\README.md:323:Or add `"includeGitInstructions": false` to `~/.claude/settings.json`. Claude Code can still run `git status` via the Bash tool when it needs context. Community-validated by [@wadabum](https://github.com/cnighswonger/claude-code-cache-fix/issues/11): 18-token cache creation across git state changes (vs thousands without the flag).
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\README.md:325:**Why we don't ship a proxy extension for this:** the proxy intercepts requests after Claude Code has already composed the system prompt — by then the volatile `git status` text is already part of the prefix that the model conditioned on in the previous turn, and stripping it post-hoc would itself bust the cache. The fix has to happen at the source. `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_GIT_INSTRUCTIONS=1` prevents the injection before the prompt is composed, which is why the native flag is the right tool. Stripping post-hoc would also remove model-visible context that an explicit Bash call can recover, and would risk false-positive matches against assistant-written text.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\README.md:414:Anthropic's prompt cache supports up to **four** `cache_control` markers per request. Claude Code currently uses three of the four; the third (between auto-injected `messages[0]` content — hooks, skills, project CLAUDE.md, deferred tools, MCP server descriptions — and the first real user content) is missing entirely. Without that marker, every change inside the auto-injected span busts the cache for everything that follows. wadabum projected ~6,500 token savings per fresh-session first turn from adding it ([anthropics/claude-code#47098](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/47098)).
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\README.md:437:After ~90 minutes idle, Claude Code's `time_based_microcompact` (and the cold-compact path triggered by `FDY()`) replaces old `tool_result` content with a sentinel string. The original content is gone for cache purposes; that part is unrecoverable from the proxy. But the sentinel itself can carry an embedded timestamp (`[Old tool result content cleared at 2026-04-30T13:42:11Z]`), which means a *second* microcompact pass against the same already-cleared position writes different bytes — busting the cache for everything after that position even though no new content was added.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\README.md:439:This extension addresses the recoverable half: normalize the sentinel to a byte-stable canonical form so repeat microcompacts don't churn the cache. **Phase 1 only** — diagnostic + opt-in normalization. Phase 2 (snapshot-and-restore of original tool_result content) is deferred to v3.5.0+ pending Phase 1 production data.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\README.md:451:- **Mode B** — prefix-only match (text begins with `[Old tool result content cleared` but does not exactly match a Mode A pattern). Mode B is **diagnostic-only**: never normalized, dump records redact to a 64-char prefix only.

Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\extension-impact-guide.md:11:**What it fixes:** Claude Code computes a `cc_version` fingerprint (e.g. `2.1.92.a3f`) from `messages[0]` content including meta/attachment blocks. Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\extension-impact-guide.md:63:### 5. `cache-control-normalize` (order 400)
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\extension-impact-guide.md:65:**What it fixes:** `cache_control` markers (the `{"type": "ephemeral"}` annotations that tell the API what to cache) can appear at inconsistent positions across turns. Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\extension-impact-guide.md:67:**ON:** Pins `cache_control` markers at canonical positions (last block of last user message).
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\extension-impact-guide.md:69:**OFF:** Marker drift between turns causes partial cache misses — not full misses, but enough to increase `cache_creation` on each turn.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\extension-impact-guide.md:73:**What it fixes:** Detects the server's cache TTL tier (1h or 5m) and ensures correct `cache_control` markers are injected. On cold starts, the server assigns 5m TTL until the first cached call promotes to 1h.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\extension-impact-guide.md:75:**ON:** Injects appropriate ephemeral markers to maximize cache reuse within the server's TTL window.

Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\extension-impact-guide.md:167:### 10. `messages-cache-breakpoint` (order 410) — opt-in via `CACHE_FIX_INJECT_MESSAGES_BREAKPOINT=1`
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\extension-impact-guide.md:169:**What it fixes:** Anthropic's prompt cache supports up to 4 `cache_control` markers per request, but Claude Code currently only places three of them. The third — at the boundary between auto-injected `messages[0]` content (hooks, skills, project CLAUDE.md, deferred-tools, MCP server descriptions) and the first real user content — is missing entirely. Without it, every change inside the auto-injected span busts the cache for everything that follows. wadabum's analysis on [anthropics/claude-code#47098](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/47098) projected ~6,500 token savings per fresh-session first turn from adding the marker.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\extension-impact-guide.md:171:**ON (`CACHE_FIX_INJECT_MESSAGES_BREAKPOINT=1`):** Runs once per request at order 410, immediately after `cache-control-normalize` (so we count markers against a normalized baseline):
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\extension-impact-guide.md:176:4. Inject `cache_control: { type: "ephemeral", ttl: "1h" }` on that block. Already-marked boundaries are not overwritten.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\extension-impact-guide.md:190:Signatures are intentionally narrow — user prose mentioning any of these tokens classifies as `user` content, not auto-injected. Under-detection means we miss the optimization on a turn; over-detection would inject mid-user-content, fragmenting the cache.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\extension-impact-guide.md:192:**Diagnostic dump (`CACHE_FIX_DUMP_MESSAGES_HEAD=<path>`):** Independent of injection. Writes a JSONL line per request capturing per-block kind, first 200 chars of text, and `cache_control` presence. Read-only — no body mutation. Provides the fixture source for verifying boundary detection in production traffic.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\extension-impact-guide.md:215:See `docs/directives/proxy-messages-cache-breakpoint.md` for the full spec.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\extension-impact-guide.md:219:**What it fixes:** When CC's `time_based_microcompact` (or the 90-minute cold-compact path via `FDY()`) fires, it replaces old `tool_result` content with a sentinel string. The original content is gone for cache purposes — that loss is unrecoverable from the proxy. But the sentinel itself may carry volatile fields (timestamps, IDs) that change between microcompact runs even when no new content was added, busting the cache for everything *after* the sentinel position. This extension normalizes the sentinel to a byte-stable canonical form so the "second microcompact, no new content" case stops churning the cache. Phase 1 only; Phase 2 (snapshot-and-restore) is deferred to v3.5.0+ pending production data from Phase 1.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\extension-impact-guide.md:223:**ON (`CACHE_FIX_NORMALIZE_MICROCOMPACT=1`):** Replaces matched sentinels with the canonical text (default `[Old tool result content cleared]` — the timestamp-stripped form). Only Mode A matches (exact match against confirmed patterns) are normalized. Mode B matches (prefix-only) are recorded in the dump but never mutated.

Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\extension-impact-guide.md:236:**Custom patterns** can be added via `CACHE_FIX_MICROCOMPACT_SENTINEL_PATTERN_<N>=<regex>` (1-indexed, sparse OK). To get the same Mode A/B treatment as defaults — including redacted prefix capture for variants of a custom family — pair each custom regex with a literal prefix via `CACHE_FIX_MICROCOMPACT_SENTINEL_PREFIX_<N>=<literal>`. The implementation can't safely derive a prefix from an arbitrary regex, so prefixes are supplied separately. Without the prefix env var, only exact-match (Mode A) capture works for that family.

Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\march-23-regression-investigation.md:68:The net prefix growth from v2.1.81 to v2.1.90 is nearly zero (+28 tokens across 9 releases). All meaningful size growth is concentrated at **v2.1.101** (+1,922 tokens in one release).
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\march-23-regression-investigation.md:83:- **System prompt** (v2.1.81 27,568 → v2.1.101 27,539) — essentially stable across 20 releases (±1.3%). The system prompt is not the source of the regression.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\march-23-regression-investigation.md:140:3. **v2.1.101 is where the real client-side growth is.** Two entirely new tools (`Monitor` and `ScheduleWakeup`) are added to every request. Every v2.1.101 user pays 6,615 chars (~1,700 tokens) of prefix on every API call to carry two tools that most of them will never invoke.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\march-23-regression-investigation.md:154:> **The Anthropic prompt cache has a 5-minute TTL.** Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\march-23-regression-investigation.md:156:> - **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for active work — checking a build, polling for state that's about to change, watching a process you just started.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\march-23-regression-investigation.md:157:> - **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, or genuinely idle.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\march-23-regression-investigation.md:159:> **Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache warmth.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\march-23-regression-investigation.md:161:This is **Anthropic's own product tooling** stating that the default cache TTL is 5 minutes. That aligns exactly with what @TigerKay1926 and others have reported in #42052 as "stuck 5m TTL." The 1-hour TTL tier exists but is opt-in via the client's `should1hCacheTTL()` GrowthBook gating — users whose client call path isn't in the allowlist get the default 5m.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\march-23-regression-investigation.md:165:1. **If the server introduced this 5m-default behavior on March 23**, users whose clients weren't on the 1h allowlist would suddenly pay full prefix rebuilds every time they idled more than 5 minutes (reading code, thinking, coffee break). This matches the user reports almost exactly.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\march-23-regression-investigation.md:166:2. **The 1h/5m tier gating is documented in the product now** — it's not a bug Anthropic is unaware of, it's a feature they've built their own long-loop tooling around. That reframes the community frustration: the behavior is *working as designed from Anthropic's side*, but the design has sharp edges for users whose sessions don't fit the cache-warm work pattern.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\march-23-regression-investigation.md:172:All four versions in this test obtained **1-hour TTL tier on Haiku** with the cache-fix interceptor active. This is because the interceptor forces `ttl: "1h"` into the `cache_control` blocks unconditionally, bypassing whatever GrowthBook allowlist gating the client would otherwise do.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\march-23-regression-investigation.md:184:1. **Server-side (March 23):** Anthropic introduced (or tightened) the 5m/1h TTL tier distinction server-side. Pre-March 23, either all calls got 1h, or the tier gating was not yet enforced. Starting March 23, clients that don't explicitly request the 1h tier (or don't match the GrowthBook allowlist) get 5m by default. Users whose workflows include any idle period >5 minutes suddenly pay full cache rebuilds they didn't pay before.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\march-23-regression-investigation.md:186:2. **Client-side (v2.1.83, March 25):** the first release after the regression. Its client diff from v2.1.81 is very small (~500 chars of tool schema changes). The regression mechanism is not in that diff. **v2.1.81 users may be getting pre-regression behavior because their client's querySource happens to be on the 1h allowlist**, or because the pre-March-23 code path emits cache_control blocks without the new tier field, which the server accepts as implicit 1h.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\march-23-regression-investigation.md:190:The practical workaround that works — pin to v2.1.81 — works because v2.1.81's client never interacts with the March 23 server-side gating in a way that penalizes it. Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\directives\proxy-microcompact-cache-stability.md:1:# Directive: microcompact cache stability
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\directives\proxy-microcompact-cache-stability.md:4:**Branch:** `directive/microcompact-cache-stability`
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\directives\proxy-microcompact-cache-stability.md:10:Stop CC's `time_based_microcompact` and 90-minute cold-compact paths from busting the prompt cache **above and beyond** the unavoidable content loss. The microcompact rewrite happens; we can't prevent it from inside the proxy. But there are two distinct cache-busting effects from a single rewrite, and we can address one of them client-side:
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\directives\proxy-microcompact-cache-stability.md:12:1. **Content loss** (unavoidable from the proxy): old tool_result content is replaced with a sentinel string. The cache for that conversation position is permanently invalidated. We accept this; only Anthropic's `CACHED_MICROCOMPACT` server flag (mentioned in CC source) can recover it.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\directives\proxy-microcompact-cache-stability.md:13:2. **Sentinel drift** (proxy-fixable): the sentinel string CC writes may differ between microcompact runs (embedded timestamps, IDs, ordering). Even when no new content is added, the rewrite alone moves bytes and busts the cache for everything *after* the sentinel position. We can normalize the sentinel to a byte-stable canonical form so that, for the unchanged-content case, repeat runs produce identical request bodies.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\directives\proxy-microcompact-cache-stability.md:21:1. **Cache TTL expired** during idle — expected, the cache just rebuilds on the next call.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\directives\proxy-microcompact-cache-stability.md:22:2. **Microcompact rewrote the conversation** — the rebuild is now for *different content* than what was previously cached, so even if cache_control markers are sticky (per `cache-control-normalize`), the position they mark has different bytes and prefix-matching falls off at the first divergence.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\directives\proxy-microcompact-cache-stability.md:24:We've already shipped `cache-control-normalize` to keep markers at canonical positions across microcompacts. That fixes marker placement but doesn't help if the underlying content at the marker position changed. The remaining client-side gap is sentinel-drift: when CC's microcompact writes a sentinel like `[Old tool result content cleared at 2026-04-30T13:42:11Z]`, the timestamp embedded in the sentinel changes every run, so even on a second microcompact pass against an already-stripped position, the bytes change and the cache busts again.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\directives\proxy-microcompact-cache-stability.md:26:If CC's sentinel turns out to be byte-stable (no embedded volatile fields), Phase 1's normalization is a no-op and we ship the diagnostic only. If the sentinel has drift, normalization recovers cache for the "no new content, just second microcompact" case — which on long-idle sessions is the common path.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\directives\proxy-microcompact-cache-stability.md:33:- `CACHED_MICROCOMPACT` — experiment flag suggesting Anthropic is working on a server-side cache-preserving variant. Track but don't depend on.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\directives\proxy-microcompact-cache-stability.md:40:- Issue #36 body — source-code function names, `keepRecent: 5`, 90-minute threshold, two-cache-bust-vector framing.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\directives\proxy-microcompact-cache-stability.md:41:- `cache-control-normalize` extension (existing, v3.0.0+) — sticky cache_control markers across rewrites; sets the baseline this directive builds on.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\directives\proxy-microcompact-cache-stability.md:50:3. New extension `proxy/extensions/microcompact-stability.mjs` registered at order 350 (between `tool-input-normalize` at 340 and `cache-control-normalize` at 400). The extension runs BEFORE `cache-control-normalize` so the latter sees the post-normalized content when computing sticky-marker hashes.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\directives\proxy-microcompact-cache-stability.md:102:**Mode B — diagnostic-only partial match.** A `tool_result` content block (or `text` item) whose text begins with the prefix `[Old tool result content cleared` BUT does NOT exactly match a Mode A pattern. This catches:
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\directives\proxy-microcompact-cache-stability.md:104:- Future CC variants we haven't seen yet (hence the prefix-only check).
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\directives\proxy-microcompact-cache-stability.md:106:Mode B matches are **NEVER normalized**. The diagnostic dump for Mode B is **redacted**: only `msg_idx`, `block_idx`, `content_kind`, `byte_length`, and a 64-char prefix of the matched text are recorded. The full text is never dumped — this protects against the case where a Mode B match is actually a CC sentinel followed by user-derived content (e.g., a tool that echoed user input back into its result).
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\directives\proxy-microcompact-cache-stability.md:108:The candidate patterns from the prior draft (`^\[Tool result truncated.*\]`, `^\[microcompact.*\]`) are **removed from the default set**: too broad, false-positive risk on tool outputs unrelated to microcompact. They can be re-added via the `CACHE_FIX_MICROCOMPACT_SENTINEL_PATTERN_<N>=<regex>` env-var family when Phase 1 data confirms a specific variant. Until then, Mode B's prefix detection is the right surface for capturing unknowns.

Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\directives\proxy-deferred-tools-restore.md:173:> **Why we don't ship a proxy extension for this:** the proxy intercepts requests after Claude Code has already composed the system prompt — by then the volatile `git status` text is already part of the prefix that the model conditioned on in the previous turn, and stripping it post-hoc would itself bust the cache. The fix has to happen at the source. `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_GIT_INSTRUCTIONS=1` prevents the injection before the prompt is composed, which is why the native flag is the right tool. Stripping post-hoc would additionally remove model-visible context that an explicit Bash call can recover, and would risk false-positive matches against assistant-written text.

This does not serialize writers, but it does preserve the important invariant: readers either see the old complete file or the new complete file, never a partial JSON blob ([proxy/extensions/prefix-diff.mjs](/home/manager/git_repos/claude-code-cache-fix/proxy/extensions/prefix-diff.mjs:144)).

Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\code-reviews\issue-87-image-guard-design-review-2026-04-27.md:15:- Pass 2’s “sum bytes across all images” rule is not sufficient to reliably prevent `413 request_too_large`. The proxy forwards `Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(reqCtx.body))` as the real payload in [proxy/server.mjs](/home/manager/git_repos/claude-code-cache-fix/proxy/server.mjs:51), so the limiting quantity is final serialized request bytes, not raw image bytes. Base64 expansion, JSON envelope overhead, system prompt size, tool schemas, and non-image blocks all count. A design that only budgets image bytes can still miss the 32 MB ceiling. The spec should require measuring `Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(body))` after each mutation step, with the image-only byte totals treated as telemetry rather than the enforcement signal.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\code-reviews\issue-87-image-guard-design-review-2026-04-27.md:20:- The current dimension helper only measures PNG and JPEG and fails open for everything else in [proxy/image-dimensions.mjs](/home/manager/git_repos/claude-code-cache-fix/proxy/image-dimensions.mjs:109). Unsupported formats such as WebP/GIF/AVIF will bypass Pass 1 and may still 4xx. The issue should call that out explicitly and decide whether v1 accepts that limitation or expands format support.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix\docs\code-reviews\issue-87-image-guard-design-review-2026-04-27.md:29:- Narrow Pass 3’s first implementation. `sharp`-only, lazy-loaded, explicit runtime error/telemetry when enabled but unavailable is better than a vague pure-JS fallback promise. Z:/repos/deps/rtk-ai__rtk\src\discover\README.md:17:**Tokenization** — The lexer (`lexer.rs`) turns the raw string into typed tokens. It's a single-pass state machine that understands shell quoting, escapes, redirects, and operators. This is critical because naive string splitting breaks on quoted content like `git commit -m "fix && update"`.
Z:/repos/deps/rtk-ai__rtk\src\discover\README.md:24:**Compound splitting** — The rewrite engine walks the tokens, splitting on `Operator` (`&&`, `||`, `;`) and `Pipe` (`|`). Each segment is rewritten independently. For pipes, only the left side is rewritten (the pipe consumer like `grep` or `head` runs raw). `find`/`fd` before a pipe is never rewritten because rtk's grouped output format breaks pipe consumers like `xargs`.

### askalf/dario README
   1: <p align="center">
   2:   <h1 align="center">dario</h1>
   3:   <p align="center"><strong>Use your Claude Pro/Max subscription with Cursor, Aider, Cline, Zed, Codex CLI, the Claude Agent SDK — any tool that speaks Anthropic or OpenAI.</strong></p>
   4:   <p align="center">A local LLM router. One endpoint, every provider. Your Claude subscription — Pro ($20), Max 5x ($100), or Max 20x ($200) — stops sitting idle in Claude Code while you pay per-token everywhere else. Speaks both the Anthropic Messages API and the OpenAI Chat Completions API at <code>http://localhost:3456</code>.</p>
   5: </p>
   6: 
   7: <p align="center">
   8:   <a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@askalf/dario"><img src="https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@askalf/dario?color=blue" alt="npm version"></a>

  20: <p align="center"><em>Zero runtime dependencies. <a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@askalf/dario">SLSA-attested</a> on every release. Nothing phones home. Independent, unofficial, third-party — see <a href="DISCLAIMER.md">DISCLAIMER.md</a>.</em></p>
  21: 
  22: > **dario is the open-source wedge of [askalf](https://askalf.org)** — the AI workforce platform we're building. Dario solves the Claude subscription problem so the rest of the workforce can run on flat-rate billing. Star this repo or follow [@ask_alf](https://x.com/ask_alf) for platform updates.
  23: 
  24: ---
  25: 
  26: ## 30 seconds
  27: 
  28: ```bash
  29: # 1. Install
  30: npm install -g @askalf/dario
  31: 
  32: # 2. Log in to your Claude subscription (Pro, Max 5x, or Max 20x)
  33: dario login                      # or `dario login --manual` for SSH / headless setups
  34: 
  35: # 3. Start the local Claude API proxy
  36: dario proxy
  37: 
  38: # 4. Point any Anthropic-compat tool at it
  39: export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3456
  40: export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=dario
  41: ```
  42: 
  43: Done. Every tool that honors those env vars — Claude Code, Cursor, Aider, Cline, Roo Code, Continue.dev, Zed, Windsurf, OpenHands, OpenClaw, Hermes, Codex CLI, the [Claude Agent SDK](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk), your own scripts — now routes through your **Claude subscription** (Pro / Max 5x / Max 20x) instead of per-token API pricing. Dario sends the same request shape Claude Code itself sends, which is the shape the subscription-billing path recognizes.
  44: 
  45: Prefer Docker? `ghcr.io/askalf/dario:latest` is a multi-arch (`linux/amd64` + `linux/arm64`) image published on every release — homelab, k8s, NAS. Full guide: [`docs/docker.md`](./docs/docker.md).
  46: 
  47: For OpenAI / Groq / OpenRouter / Ollama / LiteLLM / vLLM, add one backend line and reuse the same proxy:
  48: 
  49: ```bash
  50: dario backend add openai     --key=sk-proj-...
  51: dario backend add groq       --key=gsk_...    --base-url=https://api.groq.com/openai/v1
  52: dario backend add openrouter --key=sk-or-...  --base-url=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
  53: dario backend add local      --key=anything   --base-url=http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1
  54: 
  55: export OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3456/v1
  56: export OPENAI_API_KEY=dario
  57: ```
  58: 
  59: Switching providers is a **model-name change** in your tool — `claude-opus-4-7`, `gpt-4o`, `llama-3.3-70b`, any OpenRouter / Groq / local model — not a reconfigure. Force a specific backend with a prefix: `openai:gpt-4o`, `claude:opus`, `groq:llama-3.3-70b`, `local:qwen-coder`.
  60: 
  61: Something not right? `dario doctor` prints a single paste-ready health report. Paste that when you file an issue.
  62: 
  63: ---
  64: 
  65: ## What it actually does
  66: 
  67: You point every tool at one URL. Dario reads each request, decides which backend owns it, and forwards in that backend's native protocol.
  68: 
  69: | Client speaks | Model in request | dario routes to | What happens |
  70: |---|---|---|---|
  71: | Anthropic Messages API | `claude-*` / `opus` / `sonnet` / `haiku` | Claude backend | OAuth swap + (optional) CC template replay → `api.anthropic.com` |
  72: | Anthropic Messages API | `gpt-*`, `llama-*`, etc. | OpenAI-compat backend | Anthropic → OpenAI translation, forwarded to configured backend |
  73: | OpenAI Chat Completions | `gpt-*` / `o1-*` / `o3-*` | OpenAI-compat backend | Passthrough: auth swap, body forwarded byte-for-byte |
  74: | OpenAI Chat Completions | `claude-*` | Claude backend | OpenAI → Anthropic translation, then the Claude backend path |
  75: | Either protocol | `<provider>:<model>` | Forced by prefix | Explicit override for ambiguous names |
  76: 
  77: The tool doesn't know. The backend doesn't know. Dario is the seam.
  78: 
  79: Beyond routing, the Claude backend is a **full Claude Code wire-level template** — every observable axis (bytes, headers, body key order, TLS stack, inter-request timing, session-id lifecycle, stream-consumption shape) is captured from your installed CC binary and mirrored on outbound requests so the upstream subscription-billing path is the one the request follows. See [`docs/wire-fidelity.md`](./docs/wire-fidelity.md).
  80:

### graykode/abtop README
   1: # abtop
   2: 
   3: **Like [btop](https://github.com/aristocratos/btop), but for your AI coding agents.**
   4: 
   5: See every Claude Code and Codex CLI session at a glance — token usage, context window %, rate limits, child processes, open ports, and more.
   6: Claude Code and Codex CLI sessions are discovered from local process/file state, so multiple active profiles are supported across macOS, Linux, and Windows.
   7: 
   8: ![demo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/graykode/abtop/main/assets/demo.gif)
   9: 
  10: ## Why
  11: 
  12: - Running 3+ agents across projects? See them all in one screen.
  13: - Hitting rate limits? Watch your quota in real-time.
  14: - Agent spawned a server and forgot to kill it? Orphan port detection.
  15: - Context window filling up? Per-session % bars with warnings.
  16: 
  17: All read-only. No API keys. No auth.
  18: 
  19: ## Install
  20: 
  21: ### macOS / Linux
  22: 
  23: ```bash
  24: curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/graykode/abtop/releases/latest/download/abtop-installer.sh | sh
  25: ```
  26: 
  27: ### Cargo
  28: 
  29: ```bash
  30: cargo install abtop
  31: ```
  32: 
  33: ### Windows
  34: 
  35: Native support — no WSL required. Uses `sysinfo` for process info and `netstat -ano` for listening ports.
  36: 
  37: ```powershell
  38: powershell -c "irm https://github.com/graykode/abtop/releases/latest/download/abtop-installer.ps1 | iex"
  39: ```
  40: 
  41: Or `cargo install abtop` from any terminal with Git in PATH. Claude Code config is resolved automatically from `%USERPROFILE%\.claude`.
  42: 
  43: ### Other
  44: 
  45: Pre-built binaries for all platforms are available on the [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/graykode/abtop/releases) page.
  46: 
  47: ## Usage
  48: 
  49: ```bash
  50: abtop                    # Launch TUI
  51: abtop --once             # Print snapshot and exit
  52: abtop --setup            # Install rate limit collection hook
  53: abtop --theme dracula    # Launch with a specific theme
  54: ```
  55: 
  56: Recommended terminal size: **120x40** or larger. Minimum 80x24 — panels hide gracefully when small.
  57: 
  58: ### tmux
  59: 
  60: abtop works standalone, but running inside tmux unlocks session jumping — press `Enter` to switch directly to the pane running that agent.
  61: 
  62: ```bash
  63: tmux new -s work
  64: # pane 0: abtop
  65: # pane 1: claude (project A)
  66: # pane 2: claude (project B)
  67: # → Enter on a session in abtop jumps to its pane
  68: ```
  69: 
  70: ## Supported Agents
  71: 
  72: | Feature           | Claude Code | Codex CLI |
  73: | ----------------- | :---------: | :-------: |
  74: | Session Discovery |     ✅      |    ✅     |
  75: | Token Tracking    |     ✅      |    ✅     |
  76: | Context Window %  |     ✅      |    ✅     |
  77: | Status Detection  |     ✅      |    ✅     |
  78: | Current Task      |     ✅      |    ✅     |
  79: | Rate Limit        |     ✅      |    ✅     |
  80: | Git Status        |     ✅      |    ✅     |
