### Willxup/cpa-usage-keeper README
   1: # CPA Usage Keeper
   2: 
   3: [English README](./README.en.md)
   4: 
   5: `CPA Usage Keeper` 是一个独立的 CPA 用量持久化与可视化服务。
   6: 
   7: 它依赖 [CLIProxyAPI（CPA）](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI) 作为后端 CPA 数据来源，目标是在 CPA 之上补充持久化存储与统计分析能力。服务会从 CPA Redis usage 队列消费事件并写入 SQLite，定时拉取 CPA metadata，暴露聚合 API，并提供内置 Web Dashboard 用于查看 usage、pricing、request health 和 model/API 维度的统计信息。
   8: 
   9: ![cpa-usage-keeper-screenshot](https://images.bitskyline.com/i/2026/05/1pmg6l.png)
  10: 
  11: ## 功能特性
  12: 
  13: - CPA usage 数据持久化到 SQLite
  14: - usage 聚合 API 与 pricing API
  15: - 内置 React Dashboard
  16: - 可选密码登录保护
  17: - SQLite 数据库本地备份与保留策略
  18: - Linux systemd 服务文件
  19: - Docker / Docker Compose 部署
  20: 
  21: ## 项目结构
  22: 
  23: ```text
  24: cmd/                 应用入口
  25: internal/api/        HTTP 路由与处理器
  26: internal/app/        应用装配与启动
  27: internal/auth/       内存 session 鉴权
  28: internal/backup/     SQLite 数据库备份管理
  29: internal/config/     环境配置加载
  30: internal/cpa/        CPA 客户端与类型定义
  31: internal/models/     GORM 模型
  32: internal/poller/     后台同步轮询
  33: internal/repository/ SQLite 访问与聚合逻辑
  34: internal/service/    同步、usage 与 pricing 服务
  35: web/                 React + TypeScript 前端
  36: ```
  37: 
  38: ## 配置
  39: 
  40: 复制配置模板：
  41: 
  42: ```bash
  43: cp .env.example .env
  44: ```
  45: 
  46: | 变量 | 必填 | 默认值 | 说明 |
  47: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  48: | `CPA_BASE_URL` | 是 | - | CPA 服务地址 |
  49: | `CPA_MANAGEMENT_KEY` | 是 | - | CPA management key |
  50: | `AUTH_ENABLED` | 否 | `false` | 是否启用登录保护 |
  51: | `LOGIN_PASSWORD` | 鉴权启用时必填 | - | 登录密码 |
  52: | `AUTH_SESSION_TTL` | 否 | `168h` | Session 生命周期 |
  53: | `APP_PORT` | 否 | `8080` | HTTP 监听端口 |
  54: | `APP_BASE_PATH` | 否 | 根路径 | 子路径部署前缀，例如 `/cpa`；留空表示 `/` |
  55: | `TZ` | 否 | `Asia/Shanghai` | 项目业务时区，影响 Today、按天聚合、定时任务和日志时间 |
  56: | `REDIS_QUEUE_ADDR` | 否 | `CPA_BASE_URL` 主机名 + `8317` | CPA Redis/RESP TCP 地址；留空时会使用 `CPA_BASE_URL` 的主机名和默认端口 `8317`，且当 `CPA_BASE_URL` 为 https 时自动启用 TLS；非默认端口时填写 `host:port` |
  57: | `REDIS_QUEUE_TLS` | 否 | `false` | 是否使用 TLS 连接 Redis 队列；仅在 `REDIS_QUEUE_ADDR` 留空且 `CPA_BASE_URL` 为 https 时自动启用；如果显式设置了 `REDIS_QUEUE_ADDR`，需手动设为 `true` |
  58: | `REDIS_QUEUE_BATCH_SIZE` | 否 | `1000` | 每次最多拉取的队列记录数 |
  59: | `REDIS_QUEUE_IDLE_INTERVAL` | 否 | `1s` | 队列为空时的检查间隔 |
  60: | `REQUEST_TIMEOUT` | 否 | `30s` | CPA 请求超时 |
  61: | `TLS_SKIP_VERIFY` | 否 | `false` | 跳过 CPA HTTPS 和 Redis 队列 TLS 的证书验证；仅在使用自签名证书时启用 |
  62: | `WORK_DIR` | 否 | `./data` | 应用工作目录；数据库、日志和备份默认分别写入 `app.db`、`logs/`、`backups/` |
  63: | `LOG_LEVEL` | 否 | `info` | 日志级别 |
  64: | `LOG_FILE_ENABLED` | 否 | `true` | 是否写入持久化日志文件 |
  65: | `LOG_RETENTION_DAYS` | 否 | `7` | 日志保留天数；`0` 表示不自动清理 |
  66: | `BACKUP_ENABLED` | 否 | `true` | 是否启用 SQLite 数据库备份 |
  67: | `BACKUP_INTERVAL` | 否 | `24h` | 数据库备份间隔 |
  68: | `BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS` | 否 | `7` | 备份保留天数 |
  69: 
  70: `APP_BASE_PATH` 必须为空或以 `/` 开头；例如 `/cpa`，`/cpa/` 会规范为 `/cpa`。
  71: 
  72: 安全与数据说明：
  73: 
  74: - SQLite 数据库备份会保存应用数据库中的原始数据，备份文件不做加密。
  75: - 面向浏览器的 API 会对 key-like source/lookup 字段做脱敏或稳定公开标识映射，但不会修改数据库原始值。
  76: - 公开部署建议开启 `AUTH_ENABLED=true`，并在反向代理层配置 HTTPS。
  77: - 登录 session 存在服务进程内存中，服务重启后已登录 session 会失效。
  78: - Redis inbox 原始消息会自动清理：成功数据保留到当天结束后清理，失败数据保留 7 天。
  79: 
  80: ## 本地开发
### edouard-claude/snip README
   1: <p align="center">
   2:   <img src="https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/edouard-claude/snip?style=flat-square" alt="Release">
   3:   <img src="https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/edouard-claude/snip/ci.yaml?branch=master&style=flat-square&label=CI" alt="CI">
   4:   <img src="https://img.shields.io/github/license/edouard-claude/snip?style=flat-square" alt="License">
   5:   <img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/Go-1.25+-00ADD8?style=flat-square&logo=go" alt="Go">
   6: </p>
   7: 
   8: # snip - Reduce LLM Token Usage by 60-90%
   9: 
  10: **CLI proxy that filters shell output before it reaches your AI coding assistant's context window.** Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, Cline, Codex, Kilo Code, Antigravity, Aider, and any tool that runs shell commands.
  11: 
  12: AI coding agents burn tokens on verbose shell output that adds zero signal. A passing `go test` produces hundreds of lines the LLM will never use. `git log` dumps full commit metadata when a one-liner per commit suffices.
  13: 
  14: snip sits between your AI tool and the shell, filtering output through **declarative YAML pipelines**. Write a YAML file, drop it in a folder, done. The extensible LLM token optimizer: filters are YAML data files, not compiled code.
  15: 
  16: ```
  17:   snip — Token Savings Report
  18:   ══════════════════════════════
  19: 
  20:   Commands filtered     128
  21:   Tokens saved          2.3M
  22:   Avg savings           99.8%
  23:   Efficiency            Elite
  24:   Total time            725.9s
  25: 
  26:   ███████████████████░ 100%
  27: 
  28:   14-day trend  ▁█▇
  29: 
  30:   Top commands by tokens saved
  31: 
  32:   Command                    Runs  Saved   Savings  Impact
  33:   ─────────────────────────  ────  ──────  ───────  ────────────
  34:   go test ./...              8     806.2K  99.8%    ████████████
  35:   go test ./pkg/...          3     482.9K  99.8%    ███████░░░░░
  36:   go test ./... -count=1     3     482.0K  99.8%    ███████░░░░░
  37: ```
  38: 
  39: > Measured on a real Claude Code session — 128 commands, 2.3M tokens saved.
  40: 
  41: ## Quick Start
  42: 
  43: ```bash
  44: # Quick install (macOS/Linux)
  45: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/edouard-claude/snip/master/install.sh | sh
  46: 
  47: # Or via Homebrew
  48: brew install edouard-claude/tap/snip
  49: 
  50: # Or with Go
  51: go install github.com/edouard-claude/snip/cmd/snip@latest
  52: 
  53: # Then hook into Claude Code
  54: snip init
  55: # That's it. Every shell command Claude runs now goes through snip.
  56: ```
  57: 
  58: ## How It Works
  59: 
  60: **Before** — Claude Code sees this (689 tokens):
  61: ```
  62: $ go test ./...
  63: ok  	github.com/edouard-claude/snip/internal/cli	3.728s	coverage: 14.4% of statements
  64: ok  	github.com/edouard-claude/snip/internal/config	2.359s	coverage: 65.0% of statements
  65: ok  	github.com/edouard-claude/snip/internal/display	1.221s	coverage: 72.6% of statements
  66: ok  	github.com/edouard-claude/snip/internal/engine	1.816s	coverage: 47.9% of statements
  67: ok  	github.com/edouard-claude/snip/internal/filter	4.306s	coverage: 72.3% of statements
  68: ok  	github.com/edouard-claude/snip/internal/initcmd	2.981s	coverage: 59.1% of statements
  69: ok  	github.com/edouard-claude/snip/internal/tee	0.614s	coverage: 70.6% of statements
  70: ok  	github.com/edouard-claude/snip/internal/tracking	5.355s	coverage: 75.0% of statements
  71: ok  	github.com/edouard-claude/snip/internal/utils	5.515s	coverage: 100.0% of statements
  72: ```
  73: 
  74: **After** — snip returns this (16 tokens):
  75: ```
  76: 10 passed, 0 failed
  77: ```
  78: 
  79: That's **97.7% fewer tokens**. The LLM gets the same signal — all tests pass — without the noise.

function Get-GhCommitCount("'$repo) {
  $headers = gh api -i "repos/$repo/commits?per_page=1" 2>$null
  $link = ($headers | Select-String -Pattern '"'"'^link:|''^Link:'"' | Select-Object -First 1).ToString()
  if ("'$link -match '"'page=(\\d+)>; rel=\"last\"') { return [int]"'$Matches[1] }
  $body = ($headers | Select-String -Pattern '"'"'^'"\\[' -Context 0,200 | ForEach-Object { "'$_.Line })
  return 1
}

### README.md:1-70
   1: # claude-code-cache-fix
   2: 
   3: [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/claude-code-cache-fix?color=blue)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/claude-code-cache-fix) [![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-18%2B-green)](https://nodejs.org/) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/cnighswonger/claude-code-cache-fix)](https://github.com/cnighswonger/claude-code-cache-fix/stargazers)
   4: 
   5: English | [中文](./README.zh.md) | [한국어](./README.ko.md) | [Português](./docs/guia-pt-br.md)
   6: 
   7: Cache optimization proxy for [Claude Code](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code). Fixes prompt cache bugs that cause excessive quota burn, stabilizes the request prefix, and monitors for silent regressions. Works with all CC versions including the v2.1.113+ Bun binary.
   8: 
   9: > **v3.0.3** — Local HTTP proxy with 7 hot-reloadable extensions. A/B tested on v2.1.117: **95.5% cache hit rate through proxy vs 82.3% direct** on first warm turn. [Full release notes →](https://github.com/cnighswonger/claude-code-cache-fix/releases/tag/v3.0.0)
  10: 
  11: > **Opus 4.7 advisory:** Metered data shows 4.7 burns Q5h quota at **~2.4x the rate of 4.6** for equivalent visible token counts ([independently confirmed by @ArkNill](https://github.com/ArkNill/claude-code-hidden-problem-analysis/blob/main/16_OPUS-47-ADVISORY.md)). Two factors: a new tokenizer (up to 35% more tokens, [documented](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/whats-new-claude-4-7)) and adaptive thinking overhead (~105%, not documented in usage response). The Q5h impact compounds into **Q7d** — the weekly quota ceiling that most heavy users will hit first. Workaround: `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE_THINKING=1` reduces burn by ~3.3x but may reduce quality on complex tasks. See [Discussion #25](https://github.com/cnighswonger/claude-code-cache-fix/discussions/25) (initial observation) and [Discussion #42](https://github.com/cnighswonger/claude-code-cache-fix/discussions/42) (controlled A/B data + Q7d analysis).
  12: 
  13: ## Quick Start: Proxy (recommended)
  14: 
  15: The proxy works with any CC version — Node.js or Bun binary. It sits between Claude Code and the Anthropic API, applying cache fixes as hot-reloadable extensions.
  16: 
  17: ```bash
  18: # Install
  19: npm install -g claude-code-cache-fix
  20: 
  21: # Start the proxy (runs on localhost:9801)
  22: node "$(npm root -g)/claude-code-cache-fix/proxy/server.mjs" &
  23: 
  24: # Launch Claude Code through it
  25: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9801 claude
  26: ```
  27: 
  28: That's it. The proxy applies all 7 cache-fix extensions automatically. No wrapper scripts, no `NODE_OPTIONS`, no preload.
  29: 
  30: ### What the proxy does
  31: 
  32: On every `/v1/messages` request, 7 extensions run in order:
  33: 
  34: | Extension | What it fixes |
  35: |-----------|--------------|
  36: | `fingerprint-strip` | Removes unstable cc_version fingerprint from system prompt |
  37: | `sort-stabilization` | Deterministic ordering of tool and MCP definitions |
  38: | `ttl-management` | Detects server TTL tier, injects correct cache_control markers |
  39: | `identity-normalization` | Normalizes message identity fields for prefix stability |
  40: | `fresh-session-sort` | Fixes non-deterministic ordering on first turn |
  41: | `cache-control-normalize` | Normalizes cache_control markers across messages |
  42: | `cache-telemetry` | Extracts cache stats from response headers → `~/.claude/quota-status.json` |
  43: 
  44: Extensions are hot-reloadable — add, remove, or modify `.mjs` files in `proxy/extensions/` and changes apply to the next request without restarting. Configuration in `proxy/extensions.json`.
  45: 
  46: ### Running as a service
  47: 
  48: **Recommended (Linux/macOS) — `install-service` subcommand:**
  49: 
  50: ```bash
  51: cache-fix-proxy install-service
  52: ```
  53: 
  54: Detects your platform and writes the appropriate config:
  55: 
  56: - **Linux** → `~/.config/systemd/user/cache-fix-proxy.service` (systemd user unit)
  57: - **macOS** → `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.cnighswonger.cache-fix-proxy.plist` (launchd agent)
  58: 
  59: The output prints the next-step commands to enable and start the service. On Linux:
  60: 
  61: ```bash
  62: systemctl --user daemon-reload
  63: systemctl --user enable --now cache-fix-proxy
  64: systemctl --user enable --now cache-fix-proxy-healthcheck.timer   # auto-recovery — see below
  65: sudo loginctl enable-linger $USER   # optional: start on boot, not just on login
  66: ```
  67: 
  68: **Auto-recovery (Linux):** `install-service` also drops a healthcheck companion (`cache-fix-proxy-healthcheck.service` + `.timer`). The timer fires every 2 minutes; the oneshot service runs `curl -fs http://127.0.0.1:<port>/health` and `systemctl --user start cache-fix-proxy.service` if the probe fails. This recovers the proxy from any stop — clean or unclean, expected or unexpected — within 2 minutes. Background: `Restart=on-failure` doesn't fire on clean stops, so before this companion existed, a `systemctl stop` from any source (including unidentified ones during an Anthropic outage on 2026-04-25) would leave the proxy down indefinitely. macOS doesn't need the companion — launchd's `KeepAlive` already auto-restarts on any exit.

### README.md:214-224
 214: When you use `--resume` or `/resume` in Claude Code, the prompt cache breaks silently. Instead of reading cached tokens (cheap), the API rebuilds them from scratch on every turn (expensive). A session that should cost ~$0.50/hour can burn through $5–10/hour with no visible indication anything is wrong.
 215: 
 216: Three bugs cause this:
 217: 
 218: 1. **Partial block scatter** — Attachment blocks (skills listing, MCP servers, deferred tools, hooks) are supposed to live in `messages[0]`. On resume, some or all drift to later messages, changing the cache prefix.
 219: 
 220: 2. **Fingerprint instability** — The `cc_version` fingerprint (e.g. `2.1.92.a3f`) is computed from `messages[0]` content including meta/attachment blocks. When those blocks shift, the fingerprint changes, the system prompt changes, and cache busts.
 221: 
 222: 3. **Non-deterministic tool ordering** — Tool definitions can arrive in different orders between turns, changing request bytes and invalidating the cache key.
 223: 
 224: Additionally, images read via the Read tool persist as base64 in conversation history and are sent on every subsequent API call, compounding token costs silently.
### README.md:414-439
 414: Anthropic's prompt cache supports up to **four** `cache_control` markers per request. Claude Code currently uses three of the four; the third (between auto-injected `messages[0]` content — hooks, skills, project CLAUDE.md, deferred tools, MCP server descriptions — and the first real user content) is missing entirely. Without that marker, every change inside the auto-injected span busts the cache for everything that follows. wadabum projected ~6,500 token savings per fresh-session first turn from adding it ([anthropics/claude-code#47098](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/47098)).
 415: 
 416: The proxy can inject the missing marker on opt-in. Default off until validated against community data.
 417: 
 418: ```sh
 419: export CACHE_FIX_INJECT_MESSAGES_BREAKPOINT=1
 420: ```
 421: 
 422: The injection is conservative: it only fires when the request already carries 1–3 markers (typical CC shape) and refuses if the request is at the 4-marker limit (would 400) or has zero markers (Agent SDK / API-direct shape this extension isn't built for). Boundary detection covers all five observed auto-injected block kinds — hooks, skills, CLAUDE.md, deferred-tools, MCP — and lands the marker on the LAST auto-injected block.
 423: 
 424: A diagnostic-only env var dumps the structural shape of `messages[0]` for fixture sourcing without mutating the request:
 425: 
 426: ```sh
 427: export CACHE_FIX_DUMP_MESSAGES_HEAD=/tmp/messages-head.jsonl
 428: ```
 429: 
 430: | Env var | Default | Purpose |
 431: |---------|---------|---------|
 432: | `CACHE_FIX_INJECT_MESSAGES_BREAKPOINT` | unset | Enable breakpoint #3 injection (`=1` opt-in). |
 433: | `CACHE_FIX_DUMP_MESSAGES_HEAD` | unset | Diagnostic JSONL dump of `messages[0].content` shape — read-only, no mutation. |
 434: 
 435: ## Microcompact stability (proxy mode, opt-in)
 436: 
 437: After ~90 minutes idle, Claude Code's `time_based_microcompact` (and the cold-compact path triggered by `FDY()`) replaces old `tool_result` content with a sentinel string. The original content is gone for cache purposes; that part is unrecoverable from the proxy. But the sentinel itself can carry an embedded timestamp (`[Old tool result content cleared at 2026-04-30T13:42:11Z]`), which means a *second* microcompact pass against the same already-cleared position writes different bytes — busting the cache for everything after that position even though no new content was added.
 438: 
 439: This extension addresses the recoverable half: normalize the sentinel to a byte-stable canonical form so repeat microcompacts don't churn the cache. **Phase 1 only** — diagnostic + opt-in normalization. Phase 2 (snapshot-and-restore of original tool_result content) is deferred to v3.5.0+ pending Phase 1 production data.
### README.md:478-480
 478: - **Overage TTL downgrade** — Exceeding 100% of the 5-hour quota triggers a server-enforced TTL downgrade from 1h to 5m. This is server-side and cannot be fixed client-side. The proxy/interceptor prevents the cache instability that can push you into overage in the first place.
 479: - **Microcompact is not preventable** — The monitoring features detect context degradation but cannot prevent it. Microcompact and budget enforcement are server-controlled via GrowthBook flags with no client-side disable option.
 480: - **System prompt rewrite is experimental** — Preload-only, opt-in. Not proven to be the cause of behavior differences discussed in community reports. Use at your own risk.

### README.md:103-143
 103: ```bash
 104: # 1. Install for your AI tool
 105: rtk init -g                     # Claude Code / Copilot (default)
 106: rtk init -g --gemini            # Gemini CLI
 107: rtk init -g --codex             # Codex (OpenAI)
 108: rtk init -g --agent cursor      # Cursor
 109: rtk init --agent windsurf       # Windsurf
 110: rtk init --agent cline          # Cline / Roo Code
 111: rtk init --agent kilocode       # Kilo Code
 112: rtk init --agent antigravity    # Google Antigravity
 113: 
 114: # 2. Restart your AI tool, then test
 115: git status  # Automatically rewritten to rtk git status
 116: ```
 117: 
 118: The hook transparently rewrites Bash commands (e.g., `git status` -> `rtk git status`) before execution. Claude never sees the rewrite, it just gets compressed output.
 119: 
 120: **Important:** the hook only runs on Bash tool calls. Claude Code built-in tools like `Read`, `Grep`, and `Glob` do not pass through the Bash hook, so they are not auto-rewritten. To get RTK's compact output for those workflows, use shell commands (`cat`/`head`/`tail`, `rg`/`grep`, `find`) or call `rtk read`, `rtk grep`, or `rtk find` directly.
 121: 
 122: ## How It Works
 123: 
 124: ```
 125:   Without rtk:                                    With rtk:
 126: 
 127:   Claude  --git status-->  shell  -->  git         Claude  --git status-->  RTK  -->  git
 128:     ^                                   |            ^                      |          |
 129:     |        ~2,000 tokens (raw)        |            |   ~200 tokens        | filter   |
 130:     +-----------------------------------+            +------- (filtered) ---+----------+
 131: ```
 132: 
 133: Four strategies applied per command type:
 134: 
 135: 1. **Smart Filtering** - Removes noise (comments, whitespace, boilerplate)
 136: 2. **Grouping** - Aggregates similar items (files by directory, errors by type)
 137: 3. **Truncation** - Keeps relevant context, cuts redundancy
 138: 4. **Deduplication** - Collapses repeated log lines with counts

### README.md:316-393
 316: RTK works on Windows with some limitations. The auto-rewrite hook (`rtk-rewrite.sh`) requires a Unix shell, so on native Windows RTK falls back to **CLAUDE.md injection mode** — your AI assistant receives RTK instructions but commands are not rewritten automatically.
 317: 
 318: ### Recommended: WSL (full support)
 319: 
 320: For the best experience, use [WSL](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install) (Windows Subsystem for Linux). Inside WSL, RTK works exactly like Linux — full hook support, auto-rewrite, everything:
 321: 
 322: ```bash
 323: # Inside WSL
 324: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rtk-ai/rtk/refs/heads/master/install.sh | sh
 325: rtk init -g
 326: ```
 327: 
 328: ### Native Windows (limited support)
 329: 
 330: On native Windows (cmd.exe / PowerShell), RTK filters work but the hook does not auto-rewrite commands:
 331: 
 332: ```powershell
 333: # 1. Download and extract rtk-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip from releases
 334: # 2. Add rtk.exe to your PATH
 335: # 3. Initialize (falls back to CLAUDE.md injection)
 336: rtk init -g
 337: # 4. Use rtk explicitly
 338: rtk cargo test
 339: rtk git status
 340: ```
 341: 
 342: **Important**: Do not double-click `rtk.exe` — it is a CLI tool that prints usage and exits immediately. Always run it from a terminal (Command Prompt, PowerShell, or Windows Terminal).
 343: 
 344: | Feature | WSL | Native Windows |
 345: |---------|-----|----------------|
 346: | Filters (cargo, git, etc.) | Full | Full |
 347: | Auto-rewrite hook | Yes | No (CLAUDE.md fallback) |
 348: | `rtk init -g` | Hook mode | CLAUDE.md mode |
 349: | `rtk gain` / analytics | Full | Full |

 373: ## Configuration
 374: 
 375: `~/.config/rtk/config.toml` (macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/rtk/config.toml`):
 376: 
 377: ```toml
 378: [hooks]
 379: exclude_commands = ["curl", "playwright"]  # skip rewrite for these
 380: 
 381: [tee]
 382: enabled = true          # save raw output on failure (default: true)
 383: mode = "failures"       # "failures", "always", or "never"
 384: ```
 385: 
 386: When a command fails, RTK saves the full unfiltered output so the LLM can read it without re-executing:
 387: 
 388: ```
 389: FAILED: 2/15 tests
 390: [full output: ~/.local/share/rtk/tee/1707753600_cargo_test.log]
 391: ```

### README.md:1-100
   1: # cc-cache-audit
   2: 
   3: Claude Code v2.1.69+ injects a dynamic billing header into the system prompt that breaks cross-session prompt cache sharing. This repo contains the A/B test that proves it and the one-line fix.
   4: 
   5: ## The Fix
   6: 
   7: ```bash
   8: echo 'export CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER=false' >> ~/.zshrc
   9: source ~/.zshrc
  10: ```
  11: 
  12: Only affects new sessions. Existing ones keep running fine.
  13: 
  14: ## Root Cause
  15: 
  16: Since v2.1.69, Claude Code prepends an `x-anthropic-billing-header` string to the system prompt:
  17: 
  18: ```
  19: x-anthropic-billing-header: cc_version=2.1.88.a3f; cc_entrypoint=cli; cch=00000;
  20: ```
  21: 
  22: That `.a3f` suffix is a 3-char SHA-256 hash computed from the first user message in each conversation:
  23: 
  24: ```javascript
  25: // Deobfuscated from cli.js
  26: function computeHash(firstUserMessage, version) {
  27:   const chars = [4, 7, 20].map(i => firstUserMessage[i] || "0").join("");
  28:   return sha256("59cf53e54c78" + chars + version).slice(0, 3);
  29: }
  30: ```
  31: 
  32: Different conversation → different first message → different hash → different system prompt prefix.
  33: 
  34: This also affects **subagents within the same conversation**. Each Agent tool call has its own message context, so its first "user message" (the agent prompt) produces a different hash. Verified in a real session — 3 distinct hashes in one conversation:
  35: 
  36: ```
  37: Main conversation:  cc_version=2.1.88.a3f  (34 API calls)
  38: Subagent 1:         cc_version=2.1.88.e91  (3 API calls)
  39: Subagent 2:         cc_version=2.1.88.7c2  (3 API calls)
  40: ```
  41: 
  42: Anthropic's prompt cache uses [prefix matching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching) with no per-session isolation — cache is shared at the Organization/Workspace level. So all Claude Code sessions and subagents *should* share the same cached system prompt. But the billing header makes each one's prefix unique, causing the system prompt (~12K tokens) to get rebuilt from scratch every time.
  43: 
  44: ## A/B Test
  45: 
  46: 4 sessions per round, each with a different prompt, sequential with 8-second gaps (within the 5-min cache TTL). All sessions use `claude --print` mode.
  47: 
  48: ### Round A — Header ON (default)
  49: 
  50: | Session | Prompt | cache_read | cache_creation | hit ratio |
  51: |---------|--------|-----------|----------------|-----------|
  52: | 1 | What is the capital of France? | 11,272 | 12,206 | 48.0% |
  53: | 2 | List three prime numbers under 20. | 11,272 | 12,202 | 48.0% |
  54: | 3 | Explain what a goroutine is in one sentence. | 11,374 | 12,753 | 47.1% |
  55: | 4 | Name one benefit of TypeScript over JavaScript. | 11,272 | 12,203 | 48.0% |
  56: 
  57: Every session rebuilds ~12K tokens of cache.
  58: 
  59: ### Round B — Header OFF
  60: 
  61: | Session | Prompt | cache_read | cache_creation | hit ratio |
  62: |---------|--------|-----------|----------------|-----------|
  63: | 1 | What is the capital of France? | 23,478 | 0 | 99.98% |
  64: | 2 | List three prime numbers under 20. | 23,474 | 0 | 99.98% |
  65: | 3 | Explain what a goroutine is in one sentence. | 11,272 | 12,197 | 48.0% |
  66: | 4 | Name one benefit of TypeScript over JavaScript. | 23,475 | 0 | 99.98% |
  67: 
  68: 3 out of 4 sessions: zero cache creation, full cache read. Session 3 was a server-side cache eviction — cache came right back for session 4.
  69: 
  70: ### What the Numbers Mean
  71: 
  72: The data shows a two-tier caching pattern, consistent with the Anthropic API's cache hierarchy (`tools → system → messages`):
  73: 
  74: - **Tools block (~11,272 tokens)**: Tool definitions are stable across sessions — always cached regardless of header setting.
  75: - **System prompt block (~12,200 tokens)**: Contains the billing header with a per-session hash — rebuilt every session when header is ON.
  76: 
  77: With the header OFF, both blocks are fully cacheable → 99.98% hit ratio.
  78: 
  79: ### Cost Impact
  80: 
  81: Using Anthropic pricing (cache_read = 0.1x base, cache_creation = 1.25x base):
  82: 
  83: | | Header ON (per session) | Header OFF (per session) |
  84: |--|----------------------|------------------------|
  85: | Effective cost | 11,272×0.1 + 12,200×1.25 + 3 ≈ **16,380 equiv tokens** | 23,475×0.1 + 0 + 3 ≈ **2,351 equiv tokens** |
  86: | | baseline | **~85% reduction (~7x cheaper)** |
  87: 
  88: This measures system prompt cost only. For long conversations where user messages dominate, the relative savings decrease.
  89: 
  90: ## FAQ
  91: 
  92: **Will this get me banned?**
  93: 
  94: No reports of anyone being banned or warned. [claude-code-router](https://github.com/musistudio/claude-code-router/pull/1220) and [CLIProxyAPI](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/issues/1592) ship with this disabled in production. The env var is a proper feature toggle in the source code.
  95: 
  96: **Why did Anthropic add this?**
  97: 
  98: Internal billing attribution — tracking which Claude Code version and entrypoint (CLI, SDK, GitHub Action) made each API call. It's in the system prompt instead of HTTP headers probably because Bedrock/Vertex don't forward custom headers. The API has a `metadata` field designed for exactly this kind of thing.
  99: 
 100: **Do I need to restart existing sessions?**

  52: 
  53: ## What is Claw Compactor?
  54: 
  55: Claw Compactor is an open-source **LLM token compression engine** built around a 14-stage **Fusion Pipeline**. Each stage is a specialized compressor — from AST-aware code analysis to JSON statistical sampling to simhash-based deduplication — chained through an immutable data flow architecture where each stage's output feeds the next.
  56: 
  57: ### Demo
  58: 
  59: ```
  60: $ claw-compactor benchmark ./my-workspace
  61: 
  62:   Claw Compactor v7.0 — Fusion Pipeline Benchmark
  63:   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  64: 
  65:   Scanning workspace... 47 files, 234,891 tokens
  66: 
  67:   Stage Results:
  68:   ┌──────────────────┬──────────┬───────────┬──────────┐
  69:   │ Stage            │ Applied  │ Reduction │ Time     │
  70:   ├──────────────────┼──────────┼───────────┼──────────┤
  71:   │ Cortex           │ 47/47    │ —         │ 12ms     │
  72:   │ Photon           │ 3/47     │ 2.1%      │ 4ms      │
  73:   │ RLE              │ 41/47    │ 8.3%      │ 6ms      │
  74:   │ SemanticDedup    │ 47/47    │ 12.7%     │ 18ms     │
  75:   │ Ionizer          │ 8/47     │ 71.2%     │ 9ms      │
  76:   │ Neurosyntax      │ 23/47    │ 18.4%     │ 31ms     │
  77:   │ TokenOpt         │ 47/47    │ 4.1%      │ 3ms      │
  78:   │ Abbrev           │ 12/47    │ 6.8%      │ 5ms      │
  79:   └──────────────────┴──────────┴───────────┴──────────┘
  80: 
  81:   Summary:
  82:     Before:  234,891 tokens ($2.35 at GPT-4 rates)
  83:     After:   108,250 tokens ($1.08)
  84:     Saved:   126,641 tokens (53.9%) — $1.27/run
  85:     Time:    88ms total
  86: 
  87:   Estimated monthly savings at 100 runs/day: $3,810
  88: ```

  91: 
  92: ## How It Compares
  93: 
  94: | Feature | Claw Compactor | LLMLingua-2 | SelectiveContext | gzip + base64 |
  95: |:--------|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
  96: | Compression rate | 15–82% | 30–70% | 10–40% | 60–80% |
  97: | ROUGE-L @ 0.3 | **0.653** | 0.346 | ~0.4 | N/A |
  98: | ROUGE-L @ 0.5 | **0.723** | 0.570 | ~0.6 | N/A |
  99: | LLM inference cost | **$0** | ~$0.02/call | **$0** | **$0** |
 100: | Latency | **<50ms** | ~300ms | ~200ms | <10ms |
 101: | Reversible | **Yes** | No | No | Yes (manual) |
 102: | Content-aware routing | **14 stages** | 1 (perplexity) | 1 (self-info) | None |
 103: | AST-aware code handling | **Yes** (tree-sitter) | No | No | No |
 104: | JSON schema sampling | **Yes** | No | No | No |
 105: | Log/diff/search stages | **Yes** | No | No | No |
 106: | Required dependencies | **0** | torch, transformers | torch | zlib |
 107: | LLM-readable output | **Yes** | Partial | Partial | **No** |
 108: 
 109: **Why Claw Compactor wins:** LLMLingua-2 drops tokens by perplexity score — effective for natural language, but destroys code identifiers, JSON keys, and log patterns. Claw Compactor uses content-type-aware stages that understand the structure of what they're compressing.
 110: 
### README.md:122-150
 122: │   KV-cache    auto-detect  base64   path     simhash       JSON         │
 123: │   alignment   16 languages  strip  shorten   dedup        sampling      │
 124: │                                                                         │
 125: │  ─> LogCrunch ─> SearchCrunch ─> DiffCrunch ─> StructuralCollapse      │
 126: │        |              |              |                |                  │
 127: │    log folding    result dedup   context fold    import merge            │
 128: │                                                                         │
 129: │  ─> Neurosyntax ─> Nexus ─> TokenOpt ─> Abbrev ─────────> Output       │
 130: │        |             |          |           |                            │
 131: │    AST compress   ML token   format     NL shorten                      │
 132: │    (tree-sitter)  classify   optimize   (text only)                     │
 133: │                                                                         │
 134: │  [ RewindStore ] ── hash-addressed LRU for reversible retrieval         │
 135: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 136: ```
 137: 
 138: Key design principles:
 139: 
 140: - **Immutable data flow** — `FusionContext` is a frozen dataclass. Every stage produces a new `FusionResult`; nothing is mutated in-place.
 141: - **Gate-before-compress** — Each stage has `should_apply()` that inspects context type, language, and role before doing any work. Stages that don't apply are skipped at zero cost.
 142: - **Content-aware routing** — Cortex auto-detects content type (code, JSON, logs, diffs, search results) and language (Python, Go, Rust, TypeScript, etc.), then downstream stages make type-aware compression decisions.
 143: - **Reversible compression** — Ionizer stores originals in a hash-addressed `RewindStore`. The LLM can call a tool to retrieve any compressed section by its marker ID.

### CLAUDE.md:1-45
   1: # CLAUDE.md
   2: 
   3: This file provides guidance to Claude Code when working with this repository.
   4: 
   5: Auto Claude is an autonomous multi-agent coding framework that plans, builds, and validates software for you. It's a TypeScript-first Electron desktop application with a self-contained AI agent layer (Vercel AI SDK v6). A lightweight Python sidecar provides the optional Graphiti memory system.
   6: 
   7: > **Deep-dive reference:** [ARCHITECTURE.md](shared_docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) | **Frontend contributing:** [apps/desktop/CONTRIBUTING.md](apps/desktop/CONTRIBUTING.md)
   8: 
   9: ## Product Overview
  10: 
  11: Auto Claude is a desktop application (+ CLI) where users describe a goal and AI agents autonomously handle planning, implementation, and QA validation. All work happens in isolated git worktrees so the main branch stays safe.
  12: 
  13: **Core workflow:** User creates a task → Spec creation pipeline assesses complexity and writes a specification → Planner agent breaks it into subtasks → Coder agent implements (can spawn parallel subagents) → QA reviewer validates → QA fixer resolves issues → User reviews and merges.
  14: 
  15: **Main features:**
  16: 
  17: - **Autonomous Tasks** — Multi-agent pipeline (planner, coder, QA) that builds features end-to-end
  18: - **Kanban Board** — Visual task management from planning through completion
  19: - **Agent Terminals** — Up to 12 parallel AI-powered terminals with task context injection
  20: - **Insights** — AI chat interface for exploring and understanding your codebase
  21: - **Roadmap** — AI-assisted feature planning with strategic roadmap generation
  22: - **Ideation** — Discover improvements, performance issues, and security vulnerabilities
  23: - **GitHub/GitLab Integration** — Import issues, AI-powered investigation, PR/MR review and creation
  24: - **Changelog** — Generate release notes from completed tasks
  25: - **Memory System** — Graphiti-based knowledge graph retains insights across sessions
  26: - **Isolated Workspaces** — Git worktree isolation for every build; AI-powered semantic merge
  27: - **Flexible Authentication** — Use a Claude Code subscription (OAuth) or API profiles with any Anthropic-compatible endpoint (e.g., Anthropic API, z.ai for GLM models)
  28: - **Multi-Account Swapping** — Register multiple Claude accounts; when one hits a rate limit, Auto Claude automatically switches to an available account
  29: - **Cross-Platform** — Native desktop app for Windows, macOS, and Linux with auto-updates
  30: 
  31: ## Critical Rules
  32: 
  33: **Vercel AI SDK only** — All AI interactions use the Vercel AI SDK v6 (`ai` package) via the TypeScript agent layer in `apps/desktop/src/main/ai/`. NEVER use `@anthropic-ai/sdk` or `anthropic.Anthropic()` directly. Use `createProvider()` from `ai/providers/factory.ts` and `streamText()`/`generateText()` from the `ai` package. Provider-specific adapters (e.g., `@ai-sdk/anthropic`, `@ai-sdk/openai`) are managed through the provider registry.
  34: 
  35: **i18n required** — All frontend user-facing text uses `react-i18next` translation keys. Hardcoded strings in JSX/TSX break localization for non-English users. Add keys to both `en/*.json` and `fr/*.json`.
  36: 
  37: **Platform abstraction** — Never use `process.platform` directly. Import from `apps/desktop/src/main/platform/`. CI tests all three platforms.
  38: 
  39: **No time estimates** — Provide priority-based ordering instead of duration predictions.
  40: 
  41: **PR target** — Always target the `develop` branch for PRs, not `main`. Main is reserved for releases.
  42: 
  43: **No console.log in production code** — `console.log` output is invisible in bundled Electron apps. Use Sentry for error tracking in production; reserve `console.log` for development only.
  44: 
  45: ## Work Approach: Orchestrator-First

  15: ## 1. Codex Usage API
  16: 
  17: **Sources:** OpenAI Codex source code (`github.com/openai/codex`, Rust codebase), CodexBar macOS app (`github.com/steipete/CodexBar`), Context7 Codex developer docs.
  18: 
  19: ### 1.1 Active Polling Endpoint
  20: 
  21: ```
  22: GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage
  23: ```
  24: 
  25: Fallback (when base URL doesn't contain `/backend-api`):
  26: ```
  27: GET {base_url}/api/codex/usage
  28: ```
  29: 
  30: **Required Headers:**
  31: ```http
  32: Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
  33: ChatGPT-Account-Id: <account_id>
  34: Content-Type: application/json
  35: Accept: application/json
  36: ```
  37: 
  38: - `access_token` — The OAuth access token from `auth.openai.com` (same token our `codex-oauth.ts` already obtains)
  39: - `account_id` — Account UUID from OAuth token data. Stored in `~/.codex/auth.json` under `tokens.account_id`. Optional per CodexBar ("when available") but may be required.
  40: 
  41: ### 1.2 Response Schema
  42: 
  43: From `codex-rs/codex-backend-openapi-models/src/models/rate_limit_status_payload.rs`:
  44: 
  45: ```json
  46: {
  47:   "plan_type": "plus",
  48:   "rate_limit": {
  49:     "allowed": true,
  50:     "limit_reached": false,
  51:     "primary_window": {
  52:       "used_percent": 96,
  53:       "limit_window_seconds": 18000,
  54:       "reset_after_seconds": 673,
  55:       "reset_at": 1730947200
  56:     },
  57:     "secondary_window": {
  58:       "used_percent": 70,
  59:       "limit_window_seconds": 604800,
  60:       "reset_after_seconds": 43200,
  61:       "reset_at": 1730980800
  62:     }
  63:   },
  64:   "credits": {
  65:     "has_credits": false,
  66:     "unlimited": true,
  67:     "balance": null
  68:   },
  69:   "additional_rate_limits": [
  70:     {
  71:       "limit_name": "codex_other",
  72:       "metered_feature": "codex_other",
  73:       "rate_limit": {
  74:         "allowed": true,
  75:         "limit_reached": false,
  76:         "primary_window": {
  77:           "used_percent": 70,
  78:           "limit_window_seconds": 3600,
  79:           "reset_after_seconds": 1800,
  80:           "reset_at": 1730947200
  81:         }
  82:       }
  83:     }
  84:   ]
  85: }
  86: ```
  87: 
  88: - `primary_window` = 5h session (18000s). Maps to our `sessionPercent`.
  89: - `secondary_window` = Weekly (604800s = 7d). Maps to our `weeklyPercent`.
  90: - `reset_at` = Unix timestamp (seconds). Convert to ms for our `sessionResetTimestamp`/`weeklyResetTimestamp`.
  91: - `plan_type` values: `guest`, `free`, `go`, `plus`, `pro`, `free_workspace`, `team`, `business`, `education`, `quorum`, `k12`, `enterprise`, `edu`
  92: 
  93: ### 1.3 Passive Headers (From API Responses)
  94: 
  95: Rate limit data is also returned in HTTP response headers on every `/v1/responses` call:
  96: 
  97: ```
  98: x-codex-primary-used-percent         → float (e.g., "25.0")
  99: x-codex-primary-window-minutes       → integer (e.g., "300" for 5h)
 100: x-codex-primary-reset-at             → unix timestamp seconds
 101: x-codex-secondary-used-percent       → float (weekly)
 102: x-codex-secondary-window-minutes     → integer
 103: x-codex-secondary-reset-at           → unix timestamp seconds
 104: x-codex-credits-has-credits          → "true" or "false"
 105: x-codex-credits-unlimited            → "true" or "false"
 106: x-codex-credits-balance              → decimal string e.g. "9.99"
 107: ```
 108: 
 109: SSE event type `codex.rate_limits` also carries this data inline in streaming responses.
 110: 
 111: ### 1.4 Token Details
 112: 
 113: Our `codex-oauth.ts` already uses the correct flow:
 114: - **Client ID:** `app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann` (same as Codex CLI)
 115: - **Auth endpoint:** `https://auth.openai.com/oauth/authorize`
 116: - **Token endpoint:** `https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token`
 117: - **Scopes:** `openid profile email offline_access`
 118: - **Refresh:** `POST https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token` with `grant_type=refresh_token`
 119: 
 120: **Missing:** `account_id` for the `ChatGPT-Account-Id` header. Options:
 121: 1. Decode from the JWT access token
 122: 2. Read from `~/.codex/auth.json` (`tokens.account_id`)
 123: 3. Extract during OAuth token exchange (may be in response)
 124: 4. Try without it first (optional per CodexBar docs)

 128: ## 2. Current System Architecture
 129: 
 130: ### 2.1 Two Parallel Account Systems
 131: 
 132: The app has TWO account management systems that don't fully integrate:
 133: 
 134: **System A: Legacy Claude Profile Manager (Main Process)**
 135: - `claude-profile-manager.ts` — Manages OAuth profiles, rate limits, usage, auto-swap
 136: - `claude-profiles.json` — Stores profiles with `activeProfileId`, `accountPriorityOrder`
 137: - `usage-monitor.ts` — Polls Anthropic's `/api/oauth/usage` endpoint every 30s
 138: - `token-refresh.ts` — Refreshes tokens via `console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token`
 139: - `rate-limit-detector.ts` — Detects rate limits, triggers auto-swap
 140: - `profile-scorer.ts` — Scores profiles by availability for auto-swap

  34:  * This is NOT for authentication - only for human-readable debug identification.
  35:  *
  36:  * @param credential - The credential (token or API key) to create a fingerprint for
  37:  * @returns A safe fingerprint like "sk-ant-oa...xyz9" or "null" if no credential
  38:  */
  39: function getCredentialFingerprint(credential: string | null | undefined): string {
  40:   if (!credential) return 'null';
  41:   if (credential.length <= 16) return credential.slice(0, 4) + '...' + credential.slice(-2);
  42:   return credential.slice(0, 8) + '...' + credential.slice(-4);
  43: }

 191: ## Core Features
 192: ### Reliable Routing
 193: - <a href="https://portkey.wiki/gh-37">**Fallbacks**</a>: Fallback to another provider or model on failed requests using the LLM gateway. You can specify the errors on which to trigger the fallback. Improves reliability of your application.
 194: - <a href="https://portkey.wiki/gh-38">**Automatic Retries**</a>: Automatically retry failed requests up to 5 times. An exponential backoff strategy spaces out retry attempts to prevent network overload.
 195: - <a href="https://portkey.wiki/gh-39">**Load Balancing**</a>: Distribute LLM requests across multiple API keys or AI providers with weights to ensure high availability and optimal performance.
 196: - <a href="https://portkey.wiki/gh-40">**Request Timeouts**</a>: Manage unruly LLMs & latencies by setting up granular request timeouts, allowing automatic termination of requests that exceed a specified duration.
 197: - <a href="https://portkey.wiki/gh-41">**Multi-modal LLM Gateway**</a>: Call vision, audio (text-to-speech & speech-to-text), and image generation models from multiple providers  — all using the familiar OpenAI signature
 198: - <a href="https://portkey.wiki/gh-42">**Realtime APIs**</a>: Call realtime APIs launched by OpenAI through the integrate websockets server.
 199: 
 200: ### Security & Accuracy
 201: - <a href="https://portkey.wiki/gh-88">**Guardrails**</a>: Verify your LLM inputs and outputs to adhere to your specified checks. Choose from the 40+ pre-built guardrails to ensure compliance with security and accuracy standards. You can <a href="https://portkey.wiki/gh-43">bring your own guardrails</a> or choose from our <a href="https://portkey.wiki/gh-44">many partners</a>.
 202: - [**Secure Key Management**](https://portkey.wiki/gh-45): Use your own keys or generate virtual keys on the fly.
 203: - [**Role-based access control**](https://portkey.wiki/gh-46): Granular access control for your users, workspaces and API keys.
 204: - <a href="https://portkey.wiki/gh-47">**Compliance & Data Privacy**</a>: The AI gateway is SOC2, HIPAA, GDPR, and CCPA compliant.
 205: 
 206: ### Cost Management
 207: - [**Smart caching**](https://portkey.wiki/gh-48): Cache responses from LLMs to reduce costs and improve latency. Supports simple and semantic* caching.
 208: - [**Usage analytics**](https://portkey.wiki/gh-49): Monitor and analyze your AI and LLM usage, including request volume, latency, costs and error rates.
 209: - [**Provider optimization***](https://portkey.wiki/gh-89): Automatically switch to the most cost-effective provider based on usage patterns and pricing models.
### Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:24-69
  24: Maintain prompt cache efficiency through **exact prefix preservation** - always append new messages rather than modifying existing ones, and carefully order messages to maximize cache hits.
  25: 
  26: **Core insight**: Prompt caches only work on **exact prefix matches**. If the first N tokens of a request match a previous request, the cached computation can be reused.
  27: 
  28: **Mechanism**: Caching operates at the token level, not message level. The cache checks token-by-token for prefix matches, independent of message boundaries.
  29: 
  30: **Message ordering strategy:**
  31: 
  32: 1. **Static content first** (beginning of prompt - cached across all requests):
  33:    - System message (if server-controlled)
  34:    - Tool definitions (must be in consistent order)
  35:    - Developer instructions
  36:    - User/project instructions
  37: 
  38: 2. **Variable content last** (end of prompt - changes per request):
  39:    - User message
  40:    - Assistant messages
  41:    - Tool call results (appended iteratively)
  42: 
  43: **Configuration change via insertion:**
  44: 
  45: When configuration changes mid-conversation, **insert a new message** rather than modifying an existing one:
  46: 
  47: ```
  48: [Static prefix...]
  49: <sandbox_config_v1>     // Original config message
  50: [Conversation...]
  51: 
  52: <sandbox changed>
  53: <sandbox_config_v2>     // NEW message inserted
  54: [Conversation continues...]
  55: ```
  56: 
  57: This preserves the exact prefix of all previous messages, maintaining cache hits.
  58: 
  59: **What breaks cache hits:**
  60: 
  61: - Changing the list of available tools (position-sensitive)
  62: - Reordering messages
  63: - Modifying existing message content
  64: - Changing the model (affects server-side system message)
  65: 
  66: **Provider variations:**
  67: 
  68: - **OpenAI**: Automatic caching on exact prefix matches
  69: - **Anthropic**: Explicit cache-control headers, TTL-based invalidation (up to 5 minutes), 90% discount on cached tokens
### Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns/patterns/prompt-caching-via-exact-prefix-preservation.md:139-158
 139: **Prompt construction checklist:**
 140: 
 141: 1. **Order messages by stability**: Static → Variable
 142: 2. **Never modify existing messages**: Always append new ones
 143: 3. **Keep tool order consistent**: Enumerate tools in deterministic order
 144: 4. **Insert, don't update**: For config changes, add new messages
 145: 
 146: **Handling configuration changes:**
 147: 
 148: | Change Type | What NOT to do | What TO do |
 149: |-------------|----------------|------------|
 150: | Sandbox/approval mode | Modify permission message | Insert new `role=developer` message |
 151: | Working directory | Modify environment message | Insert new `role=user` message |
 152: | Tool list | Change mid-conversation | Avoid if possible; breaks cache |
 153: 
 154: **MCP server considerations:**
 155: 
 156: MCP servers can emit `notifications/tools/list_changed` to indicate tool list changes. **Avoid honoring this mid-conversation** as it breaks cache hits. Instead:
 157: - Delay tool refresh until conversation boundary
 158: - Or accept the cache miss as necessary trade-off

 succeeded in 488ms:

 480: 	if len(values) <= 1 {

 482: 	}

  76: 
  77: ## What it does
  78: 
  79: - **File reads (MCP)**: cached + mode-aware reads (`full`, `map`, `signatures`, `diff`, …)
  80: - **Shell output (hook)**: compresses noisy CLI output via 90+ patterns (git, npm, cargo, docker, …)
  81: - **Session memory (CCP)**: persist task/facts/decisions across chats for faster cold starts
  82: - **HTTP mode**: `lean-ctx serve` for Streamable HTTP MCP + `/v1/tools/call` (used by the Cookbook + SDK)
  83: 
  84: ## How it works (30 seconds)
  85: 
  86: ```
  87: AI tool  →  (MCP tools + shell commands)  →  lean-ctx  →  your repo + CLI
  88: ```
  89: 
  90: - **MCP server**: exposes `ctx_*` tools (read modes, caching, deltas, search, memory, multi-agent)
  91: - **Shell hook**: transparently compresses common commands so the LLM sees less noise
  92: - **CCP**: persists session state so long-running work doesn’t “cold start” every chat
  93: 
  94: ## Get started (60 seconds)
  95: 
  96: ```bash
  97: # 1) Install (pick one)
  98: curl -fsSL https://leanctx.com/install.sh | sh      # universal (no Rust needed)
  99: brew tap yvgude/lean-ctx && brew install lean-ctx    # macOS / Linux
 100: npm install -g lean-ctx-bin                          # Node.js

  95:

  98: curl -fsSL https://leanctx.com/install.sh | sh      # universal (no Rust needed)

 108:

 170: ### When to use (and when not to)
 171: 
 172: **Great fit if you…**
 173: - use AI coding tools daily and your sessions are shell-heavy (git/tests/builds)
 174: - work in medium/large repos (50+ files / monorepos)
 175: - want a local-first layer with **no telemetry by default**
 176: 
 177: **Skip it if you…**
 178: - mostly work in tiny repos and rarely call the shell from your AI tool
 179: - always need raw/unfiltered logs (you can still use `--raw`, but ROI is lower)

### graykode/abtop/README.md@1ca40d5ad33f12aa7170b7284ba7a60594c3e6ad:1-90
   1: # abtop
   2: 
   3: **Like [btop](https://github.com/aristocratos/btop), but for your AI coding agents.**
   4: 
   5: See every Claude Code and Codex CLI session at a glance — token usage, context window %, rate limits, child processes, open ports, and more.
   6: Claude Code and Codex CLI sessions are discovered from local process/file state, so multiple active profiles are supported across macOS, Linux, and Windows.
   7: 
   8: ![demo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/graykode/abtop/main/assets/demo.gif)
   9: 
  10: ## Why
  11: 
  12: - Running 3+ agents across projects? See them all in one screen.
  13: - Hitting rate limits? Watch your quota in real-time.
  14: - Agent spawned a server and forgot to kill it? Orphan port detection.
  15: - Context window filling up? Per-session % bars with warnings.
  16: 
  17: All read-only. No API keys. No auth.
  18: 
  19: ## Install
  20: 
  21: ### macOS / Linux
  22: 
  23: ```bash
  24: curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/graykode/abtop/releases/latest/download/abtop-installer.sh | sh
  25: ```
  26: 
  27: ### Cargo
  28: 
  29: ```bash
  30: cargo install abtop
  31: ```
  32: 
  33: ### Windows
  34: 
  35: Native support — no WSL required. Uses `sysinfo` for process info and `netstat -ano` for listening ports.
  36: 
  37: ```powershell
  38: powershell -c "irm https://github.com/graykode/abtop/releases/latest/download/abtop-installer.ps1 | iex"
  39: ```
  40: 
  41: Or `cargo install abtop` from any terminal with Git in PATH. Claude Code config is resolved automatically from `%USERPROFILE%\.claude`.
  42: 
  43: ### Other
  44: 
  45: Pre-built binaries for all platforms are available on the [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/graykode/abtop/releases) page.
  46: 
  47: ## Usage
  48: 
  49: ```bash
  50: abtop                    # Launch TUI
  51: abtop --once             # Print snapshot and exit
  52: abtop --setup            # Install rate limit collection hook
  53: abtop --theme dracula    # Launch with a specific theme
  54: ```
  55: 
  56: Recommended terminal size: **120x40** or larger. Minimum 80x24 — panels hide gracefully when small.
  57: 
  58: ### tmux
  59: 
  60: abtop works standalone, but running inside tmux unlocks session jumping — press `Enter` to switch directly to the pane running that agent.
  61: 
  62: ```bash
  63: tmux new -s work
  64: # pane 0: abtop
  65: # pane 1: claude (project A)
  66: # pane 2: claude (project B)
  67: # → Enter on a session in abtop jumps to its pane
  68: ```
  69: 
  70: ## Supported Agents
  71: 
  72: | Feature           | Claude Code | Codex CLI |
  73: | ----------------- | :---------: | :-------: |
  74: | Session Discovery |     ✅      |    ✅     |
  75: | Token Tracking    |     ✅      |    ✅     |
  76: | Context Window %  |     ✅      |    ✅     |
  77: | Status Detection  |     ✅      |    ✅     |
  78: | Current Task      |     ✅      |    ✅     |
  79: | Rate Limit        |     ✅      |    ✅     |
  80: | Git Status        |     ✅      |    ✅     |
  81: | Children / Ports  |     ✅      |    ✅     |
  82: | Subagents         |     ✅      |    ❌     |
  83: | Memory Status     |     ✅      |    ❌     |
  84: 
  85: ## Themes
  86: 
  87: 12 built-in themes, including 4 colorblind-friendly options (`high-contrast`, `protanopia`, `deuteranopia`, `tritanopia`). Press `t` to cycle at runtime, or launch with `--theme <name>`. Your choice is saved to `~/.config/abtop/config.toml`.
  88:

 112: 
 113: ## Configuration
 114: 
 115: `~/.config/abtop/config.toml` supports:
 116: 
 117: ```toml
 118: theme = "btop"
 119: # Hide specific agent CLIs from the TUI (case-insensitive).
 120: # Useful if you only use one agent and want a cleaner view.
 121: hidden_agents = ["codex"]
 122: # UI language. Omit or leave empty to auto-detect from LANG.
 123: language = "zh"
 124: ```
 125: 
 126: ### Supported Languages
 127: 
 128: | Code | Language            |
 129: | ---- | ------------------- |
 130: | `en` | English (default)   |
 131: | `zh` | Simplified Chinese  |
 132: 
 133: When `language` is unset, abtop auto-detects from `LANG` — any value starting with `zh` switches to Simplified Chinese, otherwise English.
 134: 
 135: ## Key Bindings
 136: 
 137: | Key                | Action                               |
 138: | ------------------ | ------------------------------------ |
 139: | `↑`/`↓` or `k`/`j` | Select session                       |
 140: | `Enter`            | Jump to session terminal (tmux only) |
 141: | `x`                | Kill selected session                |
 142: | `X`                | Kill all orphan ports                |
 143: | `t`                | Cycle theme                          |
 144: | `1`–`5`            | Toggle panel visibility              |
 145: | `Esc`              | Open/close config page               |
 146: | `q`                | Quit                                 |
 147: | `r`                | Force refresh                        |
 148:

 150:

   7: 
   8: # snip - Reduce LLM Token Usage by 60-90%
   9: 
  10: **CLI proxy that filters shell output before it reaches your AI coding assistant's context window.** Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, Cline, Codex, Kilo Code, Antigravity, Aider, and any tool that runs shell commands.
  11: 
  12: AI coding agents burn tokens on verbose shell output that adds zero signal. A passing `go test` produces hundreds of lines the LLM will never use. `git log` dumps full commit metadata when a one-liner per commit suffices.
  13: 
  14: snip sits between your AI tool and the shell, filtering output through **declarative YAML pipelines**. Write a YAML file, drop it in a folder, done. The extensible LLM token optimizer: filters are YAML data files, not compiled code.
  15: 
  16: ```
  17:   snip — Token Savings Report
  18:   ══════════════════════════════
  19: 
  20:   Commands filtered     128
  21:   Tokens saved          2.3M
  22:   Avg savings           99.8%
  23:   Efficiency            Elite
  24:   Total time            725.9s
  25: 
  26:   ███████████████████░ 100%
  27: 
  28:   14-day trend  ▁█▇
  29: 
  30:   Top commands by tokens saved
  31: 
  32:   Command                    Runs  Saved   Savings  Impact
  33:   ─────────────────────────  ────  ──────  ───────  ────────────
  34:   go test ./...              8     806.2K  99.8%    ████████████
  35:   go test ./pkg/...          3     482.9K  99.8%    ███████░░░░░
  36:   go test ./... -count=1     3     482.0K  99.8%    ███████░░░░░
  37: ```
  38: 
  39: > Measured on a real Claude Code session — 128 commands, 2.3M tokens saved.

### Willxup/cpa-usage-keeper/README.en.md@a3a988fd0dd677b789f77ecb8516926ac4b859f6:1-90
   1: # CPA Usage Keeper
   2: 
   3: [中文说明](./README.md)
   4: 
   5: CPA Usage Keeper is a standalone CPA usage persistence and dashboard service.
   6: 
   7: It relies on [CLIProxyAPI (CPA)](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI) as the backend CPA data source and adds persistent storage and statistical analysis capabilities on top of CPA. The service consumes events from the CPA Redis usage queue into SQLite, periodically pulls CPA metadata, exposes aggregation APIs, and serves a built-in web dashboard for usage, pricing, request health, and model/API statistics.
   8: 
   9: ![cpa-usage-keeper-screenshot](https://images.bitskyline.com/i/2026/05/1pmg6l.png)
  10: 
  11: ## Features
  12: 
  13: - CPA usage persistence in SQLite
  14: - Aggregated usage and pricing APIs
  15: - Built-in React dashboard
  16: - Optional password login protection
  17: - Local SQLite database backups with retention
  18: - Linux systemd service file
  19: - Docker / Docker Compose deployment
  20: 
  21: ## Project Structure
  22: 
  23: ```text
  24: cmd/                 Application entrypoint
  25: internal/api/        HTTP routes and handlers
  26: internal/app/        App wiring and startup
  27: internal/auth/       In-memory session auth
  28: internal/backup/     SQLite database backup management
  29: internal/config/     Environment config loading
  30: internal/cpa/        CPA client and types
  31: internal/models/     GORM models
  32: internal/poller/     Background sync loop
  33: internal/repository/ SQLite access and aggregations
  34: internal/service/    Sync, usage, and pricing services
  35: web/                 React + TypeScript frontend
  36: ```
  37: 
  38: ## Configuration
  39: 
  40: Copy the example config:
  41: 
  42: ```bash
  43: cp .env.example .env
  44: ```
  45: 
  46: | Variable | Required | Default | Description |
  47: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  48: | `CPA_BASE_URL` | Yes | - | CPA server URL |
  49: | `CPA_MANAGEMENT_KEY` | Yes | - | CPA management key |
  50: | `AUTH_ENABLED` | No | `false` | Enable login protection |
  51: | `LOGIN_PASSWORD` | When auth is enabled | - | Login password |
  52: | `AUTH_SESSION_TTL` | No | `168h` | Session lifetime |
  53: | `APP_PORT` | No | `8080` | HTTP listen port |
  54: | `APP_BASE_PATH` | No | root path | Subpath prefix such as `/cpa`; empty means `/` |
  55: | `TZ` | No | `Asia/Shanghai` | Project business timezone; affects Today, daily aggregation, scheduled tasks, and log timestamps |
  56: | `REDIS_QUEUE_ADDR` | No | `CPA_BASE_URL` hostname + `8317` | CPA Redis/RESP TCP address; when empty, uses the `CPA_BASE_URL` hostname with port `8317` and auto-detects TLS from whether `CPA_BASE_URL` is https; set `host:port` for non-default ports |
  57: | `REDIS_QUEUE_TLS` | No | `false` | Use TLS for Redis queue connection; when `REDIS_QUEUE_ADDR` is set explicitly, enable this with `true` to use TLS |
  58: | `REDIS_QUEUE_BATCH_SIZE` | No | `1000` | Maximum queue records per pull |
  59: | `REDIS_QUEUE_IDLE_INTERVAL` | No | `1s` | Empty queue check interval |
  60: | `REQUEST_TIMEOUT` | No | `30s` | CPA request timeout |
  61: | `TLS_SKIP_VERIFY` | No | `false` | Skip TLS certificate verification for CPA HTTPS and Redis queue TLS; enable only with self-signed certificates |
  62: | `WORK_DIR` | No | `./data` | Application work directory; database, logs, and backups default to `app.db`, `logs/`, and `backups/` under it |
  63: | `LOG_LEVEL` | No | `info` | Log level |
  64: | `LOG_FILE_ENABLED` | No | `true` | Write persistent log files |
  65: | `LOG_RETENTION_DAYS` | No | `7` | Log retention days; `0` disables cleanup |
  66: | `BACKUP_ENABLED` | No | `true` | Enable SQLite database backups |
  67: | `BACKUP_INTERVAL` | No | `24h` | Database backup interval |
  68: | `BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS` | No | `7` | Backup retention days |
  69: 
  70: `APP_BASE_PATH` must be empty or start with `/`; for example `/cpa`. `/cpa/` is normalized to `/cpa`.
  71: 
  72: Security and data notes:
  73: 
  74: - SQLite database backups store original data from the application database, and backup files are not encrypted.
  75: - Browser-facing APIs redact key-like source/lookup fields or map them to stable public identifiers, but raw database values are unchanged.
  76: - For public deployments, enable `AUTH_ENABLED=true` and terminate HTTPS at your reverse proxy.
  77: - Login sessions are stored in process memory and become invalid after restart.
  78: - Redis inbox raw messages are cleaned up automatically: successful rows are kept until the end of the current day, and failed rows are kept for 7 days.
  79:

### askalf/dario/README.md@0271f87309ea8ff17dae9111409392ddec563e0f:65-125
  65: ## What it actually does
  66: 
  67: You point every tool at one URL. Dario reads each request, decides which backend owns it, and forwards in that backend's native protocol.
  68: 
  69: | Client speaks | Model in request | dario routes to | What happens |
  70: |---|---|---|---|
  71: | Anthropic Messages API | `claude-*` / `opus` / `sonnet` / `haiku` | Claude backend | OAuth swap + (optional) CC template replay → `api.anthropic.com` |
  72: | Anthropic Messages API | `gpt-*`, `llama-*`, etc. | OpenAI-compat backend | Anthropic → OpenAI translation, forwarded to configured backend |
  73: | OpenAI Chat Completions | `gpt-*` / `o1-*` / `o3-*` | OpenAI-compat backend | Passthrough: auth swap, body forwarded byte-for-byte |
  74: | OpenAI Chat Completions | `claude-*` | Claude backend | OpenAI → Anthropic translation, then the Claude backend path |
  75: | Either protocol | `<provider>:<model>` | Forced by prefix | Explicit override for ambiguous names |
  76: 
  77: The tool doesn't know. The backend doesn't know. Dario is the seam.
  78: 
  79: Beyond routing, the Claude backend is a **full Claude Code wire-level template** — every observable axis (bytes, headers, body key order, TLS stack, inter-request timing, session-id lifecycle, stream-consumption shape) is captured from your installed CC binary and mirrored on outbound requests so the upstream subscription-billing path is the one the request follows. See [`docs/wire-fidelity.md`](./docs/wire-fidelity.md).
  80: 
  81: ---
  82: 
  83: ## Cost comparison
  84: 
  85: Claude subscription tiers: **Pro** ($20/mo) · **Max 5x** ($100/mo) · **Max 20x** ($200/mo). Dario routes through whichever you have — pick by your usage volume, not by what dario needs.
  86: 
  87: | Setup | Monthly cost (heavy single-tool user) |
  88: |---|---|
  89: | Cursor + Anthropic API direct | $80–$300 |
  90: | Cursor + ChatGPT Plus | $20 + per-token overage |
  91: | **Cursor + Claude Pro/Max + dario** | **$20 (Cursor) + $20–200 (your Claude tier) flat — every Claude call routes through your subscription** |
  92: | Multi-tool heavy use (Cursor + Aider + Cline + Continue) without dario | $200–$600+ |
  93: | **Same multi-tool use with dario** | **$20–200 flat — one Pro/Max subscription routes all of them** |
  94: 
  95: Already have **Pro + Max** stacked? Pool mode (`dario accounts add work` / `dario accounts add personal`) routes across both, with session stickiness keeping multi-turn agents pinned to one account so the prompt cache survives. Tiers mix freely — dario only cares about headroom, not which plan an account is on.
  96: 
  97: ---
  98: 
  99: ## Why you'll install this
 100: 
 101: - **One URL for every provider.** Cursor, Aider, Continue, Zed, OpenHands, Claude Code, your own scripts — every tool you own has its own per-provider config. Dario collapses that into a single `localhost:3456` that speaks both Anthropic and OpenAI protocols and routes by model name.
 102: - **Your Claude subscription stops sitting idle.** Cursor, Aider, Zed, Continue all want API keys and bill per-token while your Pro / Max 5x / Max 20x plan only gets used in Claude Code. Dario routes them through your plan via Claude Code's exact wire shape.
 103: - **You hit rate limits on long agent runs.** Add a second / third Claude subscription with `dario accounts add work` and pool mode routes each request to whichever account has the most headroom. Session stickiness pins multi-turn conversations; in-flight 429 failover retries on a different account before your client sees the error. See [`docs/multi-account-pool.md`](./docs/multi-account-pool.md).
 104: - **You run a coding agent that isn't Claude Code.** Cline, Roo Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Continue.dev, GitHub Copilot, OpenHands, OpenClaw, Hermes, hands — dario's universal `TOOL_MAP` (66 schema-verified entries) pre-maps their tool names to Claude Code's native set. No flag, no validator errors. See [`docs/agent-compat.md`](./docs/agent-compat.md).
 105: - **You want the proxy off the wire entirely.** Shim mode is an in-process `globalThis.fetch` patch — no HTTP hop, no port to bind, no `BASE_URL`. `dario shim -- claude --print "hi"` and CC thinks it's talking directly to `api.anthropic.com`. See [`docs/shim.md`](./docs/shim.md).
 106: - **You want CC's behavioral constraints out of your prompt.** `dario proxy --system-prompt=partial` strips CC's Tone-and-style / Text-output / verbosity / no-comments-by-default bullets and recovers ~1.2–2.8× output capability on open-ended work — empirically without flipping subscription billing (the classifier doesn't read this slot). RLHF refusals on harmful content are unaffected (alignment is in the weights, not the prompt). See [`docs/system-prompt.md`](./docs/system-prompt.md) and the empirical writeup in [`docs/research/system-prompt.md`](./docs/research/system-prompt.md).
 107: - **You want dario reachable from inside Claude Code or any MCP client.** `dario subagent install` registers a CC sub-agent for in-session diagnostics ([`docs/sub-agent.md`](./docs/sub-agent.md)). `dario mcp` turns dario into a read-only MCP server ([`docs/mcp-server.md`](./docs/mcp-server.md)).
 108: - **You want to actually audit it.** ~13,170 lines of TypeScript across 28 files. Zero runtime dependencies. Credentials at `~/.dario/` with `0600` permissions. `127.0.0.1`-only by default. Every release [SLSA-attested](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@askalf/dario). Nothing phones home. Small enough to read in a weekend.
 109: - **You want a deep-research tool that runs at $0/mo.** [deepdive](https://github.com/askalf/deepdive) is dario's companion CLI — `npx @askalf/deepdive "your question"`, get a cited Markdown report. Replaces Perplexity Pro ($20/mo), OpenAI Deep Research ($20/mo), Gemini Deep Research ($20/mo) — all of which mark up LLM calls on top of LLM calls. The deep-research workload (50k–200k tokens per question, sustained) is exactly what Max was priced for; deepdive is what uses it for that.

 136: ## Who this is for
 137: 
 138: **Best fit:**
 139: 
 140: - Developers using multiple LLMs across multiple tools tired of juggling base URLs, keys, and per-tool provider configs.
 141: - Claude Pro / Max subscribers who want their subscription usable from every tool on their machine, not just Claude Code.
 142: - Teams running local or hosted OpenAI-compat servers (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama, Groq, OpenRouter, self-hosted) who want one stable local endpoint every tool can reuse.
 143: - [Claude Agent SDK](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk) users who want OAuth-subscription routing under the SDK. Point `baseURL: 'http://localhost:3456'` and dario translates API-key calls into your Claude subscription auth — agent code stays identical.
 144: - Power users on multi-agent workloads who want multi-account pooling, session stickiness, and in-flight 429 failover on their own machine, against their own subscriptions.
 145: 
 146: **Not a fit:**
 147: 
 148: - You need vendor-managed production SLAs on every request. Use the provider APIs directly.
 149: - You need a hosted, multi-tenant, managed routing platform with a dashboard, team auth, and support contracts. Dario is a local, single-user tool — the [askalf platform](https://askalf.org) is the right surface for the team / fleet case.
 150: - You want a chat UI. Use claude.ai or chatgpt.com.
 151: 
 152: ---
 153: 
 154: ## Backends
 155: 
 156: Dario's routing is organized around **backends**. Each is a swappable adapter — add one, your tools reach it through `localhost:3456` in whichever API shape they already speak. Run zero, one, or all concurrently.
 157: 
 158: ### 1. OpenAI-compat backend
 159: 
 160: Any provider that speaks the OpenAI Chat Completions API.
 161: 
 162: ```bash
 163: dario backend add openai     --key=sk-proj-...
 164: dario backend add groq       --key=gsk_...   --base-url=https://api.groq.com/openai/v1
 165: dario backend add openrouter --key=sk-or-... --base-url=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
 166: dario backend add local      --key=anything  --base-url=http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1
 167: ```
 168: 
 169: Credentials live at `~/.dario/backends/<name>.json` with mode `0600`. Body forwarded as-is, only the `Authorization` header is swapped, streaming forwarded byte-for-byte. Force a specific backend with a [provider prefix](./docs/usage.md#provider-prefix) on the model field.
 170: 
 171: ### 2. Claude subscription backend
 172: 
 173: OAuth-backed Claude Pro / Max 5x / Max 20x, billed against your plan instead of the API. Activated by `dario login` (or `dario login --manual` for SSH / container setups, v3.20). Any tier with Claude Code access works — see [`docs/faq.md`](./docs/faq.md).
 174: 
 175: Every outbound Claude request is rebuilt to match a request Claude Code itself would make — system prompt, tool definitions, identity headers, billing tag, beta flags, header insertion order, static header values, `anthropic-beta` flag set, top-level request-body key order — using a live-extracted template from your actually-installed CC binary that self-heals on every upstream CC release.
 176: 
 177: Key mechanisms in brief: live template extraction from your installed `claude` binary, drift detection with forced refresh on mismatch, OAuth config auto-detection (so dario picks up Anthropic-side rotations on the next run), atomic cache writes, framework scrubbing (third-party identity markers stripped from system prompt), Bun auto-relaunch (so the TLS ClientHello matches CC's runtime). `dario proxy --passthrough` does an OAuth swap and nothing else — use it when the upstream tool already builds a Claude-Code-shaped request.
 178: 
 179: What this addresses: per-request fidelity. What it can't address alone: cumulative per-OAuth-session aggregates. The v3.22 – v3.28 wire-fidelity track closed six of those axes (body order, TLS, pacing, stream-drain, session-id lifecycle, MCP/sub-agent surface — see [`docs/wire-fidelity.md`](./docs/wire-fidelity.md)); for anything left, [pool mode](./docs/multi-account-pool.md) distributes load across multiple subscriptions.
 180: 
 181: ---
 182: 
 183: ## Multi-account pool mode
 184: 
 185: Pool mode activates automatically when `~/.dario/accounts/` contains 2+ accounts. Each request picks the account with the highest headroom; multi-turn agent sessions pin to one account so the Anthropic prompt cache survives; in-flight 429s retry on a different account before the client sees an error.

Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns\research\ai-accelerated-learning-and-skill-development-report.md:11:This report investigates educational frameworks, learning science principles, and academic literature applicable to AI-accelerated learning and skill development. The research identified foundational learning science concepts (spaced repetition, deliberate practice, feedback loops), AI tutor design patterns, cognitive science frameworks (Bloom's 2 Sigma Problem, Cognitive Load Theory, Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development), scaffolding and metacognition frameworks, and educational technology standards. Academic literature review (2022-2025) analyzed 58+ peer-reviewed studies and large-scale empirical studies involving 100,000+ developers, revealing consistent findings about productivity gains (15-35%) alongside concerns about superficial learning. Key findings include the strong empirical support for AI tutoring systems that combine adaptive scaffolding with fading support, metacognitive development features, and cognitive load-aware prompting. Formal frameworks identified include ITS architecture evolution, Human-AI Co-Learning patterns, System-Driven Learning, and the Skill Leveling Effect.

Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns\research\subagent-compilation-checker-report.md:560:### CriticGPT-Style Code Review
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns\research\subagent-compilation-checker-report.md:562:**Description**: Deploy specialized AI models trained specifically for code critique and evaluation. These models act as automated code reviewers that identify bugs, detect security vulnerabilities, suggest improvements, verify correctness, and check adherence to coding standards.
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns\research\subagent-compilation-checker-report.md:564:**Relationship to Subagent Compilation Checker**: Both patterns use a separate verification agent to validate work before it reaches production. CriticGPT focuses on semantic quality (bugs, security, best practices) while Subagent Compilation Checker focuses on syntactic correctness (build errors, compilation failures). Both return structured error reports rather than full context, and both can be integrated into iterative improvement loops.
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns\research\subagent-compilation-checker-report.md:566:**Key Differences**: CriticGPT is specialized for semantic code review requiring domain-specific training, while Subagent Compilation Checker handles technical build processes. CriticGPT typically runs after compilation succeeds, while the compilation checker runs as a prerequisite.
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns\research\subagent-compilation-checker-report.md:574:**Description**: Develop AI-powered tools specifically designed to assist humans in reviewing and verifying code, whether AI-generated or human-written. This includes agents that analyze code changes, summarize intent, explain decisions, and ensure alignment with user expectations.
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns\research\subagent-compilation-checker-report.md:576:**Relationship to Subagent Compilation Checker**: Both patterns address the bottleneck of verification as AI generates more code. Both emphasize the importance of efficient review processes and structured feedback. Subagent Compilation Checker automates the technical verification (does it compile?), while AI-assisted code review focuses on semantic verification (is it correct and aligned with intent?).
Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns\research\subagent-compilation-checker-report.md:578:**Key Differences**: AI-Assisted Code Review emphasizes human-in-the-loop collaboration and explainability, while Subagent Compilation Checker is fully automated. One focuses on helping humans review faster, the other on preventing build errors from reaching the main agent context.

Z:/repos/deps/awesome-agentic-patterns\research\versioned-constitution-governance-report.md:11:Versioned Constitution Governance is a pattern for managing AI agent behavior through version-controlled, signed policy documents. This pattern addresses the critical need for auditability, traceability, and controlled evolution of AI agent governance policies. By treating constitutions (rule sets governing agent behavior) as code with version control, cryptographic signing, and formal review gates, organizations can ensure that safety regressions are detectable, policy changes are attributable, and rapid rollback of problematic changes is possible.

Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix/CHANGELOG.md:158:- **BUGFIX: TTL ordering violation causes 400 error at Q5h=100%** — When the user's quota hit 100%, CC places `ttl: "5m"` markers. Our interceptor then added `ttl: "1h"` markers on other blocks, violating Anthropic's ordering constraint (1h cannot follow 5m in tools→system→messages order). Fix: detect existing TTL tier from the payload before any extension runs. If any block has `ttl: "5m"`, all injected markers (TTL injection, `cache_control_normalize`, `cache_control_sticky`) now use `5m` to match. Reported by @cowwoc (#44).

Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix/CHANGELOG.md:178:- **BUGFIX: `cache_control_sticky` exceeded Anthropic's 4-marker limit** — Reduced `MAX_POSITIONS` from 3 to 2. With 1 system marker + 1 canonical from `cache_control_normalize` + 3 historical = 5, exceeding Anthropic's hard limit of 4 `cache_control` blocks per request. Caused `400 invalid_request_error` on sessions with enough history to fill all 3 slots. Now: 1 system + 1 canonical + 2 historical = 4.
Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix/CHANGELOG.md:182:- **`cache_control_sticky`** — Preserves historical `cache_control` marker positions across turns. CC maintains one user-side marker at a time, dropping previous positions (~43 bytes of JSON framing per dropped position). On long sessions this causes tail-of-message byte drift that invalidates downstream cached blocks. This extension tracks up to 2 historical marker positions by stable message hash and reinstates them on subsequent turns (2 historical + 1 canonical from normalize + 1 system = 4, Anthropic's hard limit). Runs after `cache_control_normalize`. Credit: [@deafsquad](https://github.com/deafsquad) (PR #33).

Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix/CHANGELOG.md:192:- **`smoosh_split`** — Universal un-smoosh: peels any trailing `<system-reminder>` content out of `tool_result.content` strings back into standalone text blocks. Reverses CC's `smooshSystemReminderSiblings` folding that causes per-turn byte drift in tool results. Defaults ON. Credit: [@deafsquad](https://github.com/deafsquad) (PR #26).

Z:/repos/deps/cnighswonger-claude-code-cache-fix/README.md:11:> **Opus 4.7 advisory:** Metered data shows 4.7 burns Q5h quota at **~2.4x the rate of 4.6** for equivalent visible token counts ([independently confirmed by @ArkNill](https://github.com/ArkNill/claude-code-hidden-problem-analysis/blob/main/16_OPUS-47-ADVISORY.md)). Two factors: a new tokenizer (up to 35% more tokens, [documented](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/whats-new-claude-4-7)) and adaptive thinking overhead (~105%, not documented in usage response). The Q5h impact compounds into **Q7d** — the weekly quota ceiling that most heavy users will hit first. Workaround: `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE_THINKING=1` reduces burn by ~3.3x but may reduce quality on complex tasks. See [Discussion #25](https://github.com/cnighswonger/claude-code-cache-fix/discussions/25) (initial observation) and [Discussion #42](https://github.com/cnighswonger/claude-code-cache-fix/discussions/42) (controlled A/B data + Q7d analysis).
